1. Bài đánh giá tổng hợp yêu cầu kiểm soát toàn bộ khẩu hình đã học từ Module 1 đến Module 3. Khi thực hiện, chú ý mở khẩu hình chuẩn xác cho các nguyên âm đơn, đặt vị trí lưỡi chuẩn cho các phụ âm khó, và nhấn đúng trọng âm từ. Duy trì luồng hơi liên tục từ cơ bụng để nối các phụ âm cuối với nguyên âm đầu từ tiếp theo một cách mượt mà, đảm bảo độ chuẩn xác và tự nhiên cao nhất.

Evaluation /ɪˌvæl.juˈeɪ.ʃən/ (sự định giá, đánh giá năng lực)
Mastery /ˈmæs.tɚ.i/ (sự thuần thục, làm chủ)
Consistency /kənˈsɪs.tən.si/ (sự kiên định, tính nhất quán)
Phonetics /fəˈnet̬.ɪks/ (ngữ âm học).
3. Practice Sentences:
- Regular evaluation helps track your continuous growth and phonetic mastery.
- The student demonstrated great consistency in pronouncing difficult word endings.

data.title: Bài 63: Hòa hợp chủ ngữ - động từ (Subject-Verb Agreement)
data.theory:
1. Quy tắc cơ bản: S số ít + Vs/es, S số nhiều + V0. He lives, They live.
2. Each, Every, Everyone, Somebody, Nobody, No one, Either, Neither + V số ít: Everyone is here. Each student has a laptop.
3. Both, Many, Few + V số nhiều: Both are good. Many people are waiting.
4. Chủ ngữ dài: Động từ chia theo chủ ngữ CHÍNH, không theo danh từ xen giữa: The book on the tables is mine (chia theo book, không phải tables). The man who lives next door is... (chia theo man)
5. There is/are chia theo N sau nó: There is a book, There are two books.
6. The number of + N số nhiều + V số ít (Số lượng...) vs A number of + N số nhiều + V số nhiều (Một số...): The number of students is increasing vs A number of students are waiting.
data.examples:
1. My collection of old stamps is very valuable. I have collected them for 10 years.
   (Bộ sưu tập tem cũ của tôi rất giá trị - chia theo collection, không phải stamps)
2. Everyone in my family is very supportive and kind.
   (Mọi người trong gia đình tôi đều rất ủng hộ và tốt bụng - Everyone + is)
3. There are a lot of interesting books in this library. You should come here.
   (Có rất nhiều sách thú vị trong thư viện này - There are + số nhiều)
4. A number of people are waiting outside. They want to meet the manager.
   (Một số người đang đợi bên ngoài - A number of + are)
5. The number of cars in the city is increasing rapidly. That's why there's so much traffic.
   (Số lượng ô tô trong thành phố đang tăng nhanh - The number of + is)

Đầu lưỡi áp sát vào lợi trên, chặn luồng hơi trong miệng, đẩy luồng hơi thoát hoàn toàn qua mũi và làm rung dây thanh quản.
​Đánh vần ghép âm:
N - o: đọc là: No /nəʊ/
N - i_e - c - e: đọc là: Nice /naɪs/
N - i - g - h - t: đọc là: Night /naɪt/
S - u - n: đọc là: Sun /sʌn/
L - ear - n: đọc là: Learn /lɜːn/.
​Từ vựng và ý nghĩa:
No: Không.
Nice: Đẹp, tuyệt.
Night: Ban đêm.
Sun: Mặt trời.
Learn: Học tập.

data.title: Bài 2: Âm /e/ và /ɪ/ ngắn, bắt đầu với  im-, in-, ill-, ir-, đuôi có -ic, -id", -ish, -it, y đứng giữa. Nguyên âm đơn Monophthongs

Âm: e ngắn, Âm: ɪ: i ngắn.Nguyên âm đơn: Monophthongs.
Âm e mở miệng vừa phải đọc như e; âm i ngắn thả lỏng môi, không căng mép, phát âm giật hơi dứt khoát nằm ở khoảng giữa âm i và âm ê.
​Đánh vần ghép âm:
B - e - d: đọc là: Bed /bed/
R - e - d: đọc là: Red /red/
S - i - t: đọc là: Sit /sɪt/
P - i - n: đọc là: Pin /pɪn/
P - i - g: đọc là: Pig /pɪɡ/.
​Từ vựng và ý nghĩa:
Bed: Cái giường.
Red: Màu đỏ.
Sit: Ngồi.
Pin: Cái ghim.
Pig: Con lợn.
​Câu thực hành: The red pin is near the big pig.

data.title: Bài 64: There is/are vs It is
data.theory:
1. There is/are = Có... ở đâu đó (tồn tại): There is a book on the table (Có một cuốn sách trên bàn). There are many people waiting.
2. It is = Nó là... (thời gian, thời tiết, khoảng cách, ý kiến): It is 7 AM, It is raining, It is 5 km from here to school, It is difficult to learn English.
3. Phân biệt: There is a lot of rain (Có nhiều mưa - tồn tại) vs It is raining a lot (Trời đang mưa nhiều - thời tiết)
4. Cấu trúc hay: There seems/appears to be + N (Dường như có...): There seems to be a problem.
data.examples:
1. There is a small cafe near my office. The coffee there is excellent.
   (Có một quán cà phê nhỏ gần văn phòng tôi. Cà phê ở đó rất ngon.)
2. It is very difficult to find a parking space in this area during rush hour.
   (Rất khó tìm chỗ đỗ xe ở khu vực này vào giờ cao điểm - It is + adj + to V)
3. There are too many cars on the road today. That's why we are stuck in traffic.
   (Hôm nay có quá nhiều ô tô trên đường. Đó là lý do kẹt xe.)
4. It is 10 kilometers from my house to the nearest supermarket.
   (Từ nhà tôi đến siêu thị gần nhất là 10km - It is + khoảng cách)
5. Is there anything I can do to help you? - No, thanks. I'm fine.
   (Có gì tôi giúp được không? - Không, cảm ơn. Tôi ổn.)

data.title: Bài 104: Âm e ngắn và i ngắn
data.transcript:
​👈 Click on the speaker icon to listen! Under "Step 1"
​Make the sound short and quick: e, ih.

​How to say these sounds:
For short E, open your mouth moderately and relax your lips.

For short I, keep your lips completely relaxed without stretching, and pronounce a quick, crisp sound between "i" and "ê".

​Letter rules:
Look for "e" in short single-syllable words like Bed, Red, and Pen.

Look for "i" in single-syllable words like Sit, Pin, and Pig.

Look for prefixes starting with "im-", "in-", "ill-", and "ir-" like Import, Infant, Illness, and Irrigate.

Look for suffixes ending in "-ic", "-id", "-ish", and "-it" like Music, Vivid, Finish, and Rabbit.

Look for "y" in the middle of words like Gym, System, Lyric, and Myth.

Look for unstressed "e" or "a" in words like Begin, Decide, Market, Village, and Luggage.

​Word examples and meanings:

Bed: a piece of furniture for sleep. (Cái giường)

Red: the color of blood or a tomato. (Màu đỏ)

Pen: a tool used for writing with ink. (Cây bút)

Sit: to rest your body on a chair. (Ngồi)

Pin: a small sharp metal pin. (Cái ghim)

Pig: a farm animal with a pink body. (Con lợn)

Miss: to feel sad when someone is not there. (Bỏ lỡ, nhớ)

Import: to bring goods into a country. (Nhập khẩu)

Infant: a very young child or baby. (Trẻ sơ sinh)

Illness: the state of being sick or ill. (Bệnh tật)

Irrigate: to supply water to land or crops. (Tưới tiêu)

Music: vocal or instrumental sounds combined. (Âm nhạc)

Vivid: producing powerful feelings or clear images. (Sống động)

Finish: to bring something to an end. (Hoàn thành)

Rabbit: a small animal with long ears. (Con thỏ)

Gym: a room or building for physical exercise. (Phòng tập)

System: a set of connected things or parts. (Hệ thống)

data.title: Bài 39: Âm /ŋ/ (ng)
data.transcript:
Hướng dẫn khẩu hình: Âm: ŋ: ng.
Cuống lưỡi nâng lên chạm vào vòm họng mềm, chặn không cho luồng hơi thoát ra qua miệng, đẩy hơi thoát qua mũi và làm rung dây thanh quản.
​Đánh vần ghép âm:
S - i - ng: đọc là: Sing /sɪŋ/
L - o - ng: đọc là: Long /lɒŋ/
M - o - r - n - i - ng: đọc là: Morning /ˈmɔːnɪŋ/
E - n - g - l - i - sh: đọc là: English /ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/
Th - i - ng: đọc là: Thing /θɪŋ/.
​Từ vựng và ý nghĩa:
Sing: Hát.
Long: Dài.
Morning: Buổi sáng.
English: Tiếng Anh.
Thing: Sự vật, đồ vật.
​Câu thực hành: Sing a long song in the morning in English about things.
​Lưu ý: Âm :ng: là âm mũi hữu thanh, giữ nguyên cuống lưỡi chạm vòm mềm và không bật thêm âm g ở phía sau.

data.title: Bài 40: Âm /h/ (h)

Mở miệng tự nhiên theo âm tiết tiếp theo, đẩy luồng hơi xát nhẹ qua khe thanh môn ra ngoài, không làm rung dây thanh quản.
​Đánh vần ghép âm:
H - e - l - l - o: đọc là: Hello /həˈləʊ/
H - ou - s - e: đọc là: House /haʊs/
H - a - p - p - y: đọc là: Happy /ˈhæpi/
H - ow: đọc là: How /haʊ/
Wh - o: đọc là: Who /huː/.
​Từ vựng và ý nghĩa:
Hello: Xin chào.
House: Ngôi nhà.
Happy: Vui vẻ.
How: Như thế nào.
Who: Ai.
​Câu thực hành: Hello, happy house, how are you? Who is there?
​Lưu ý: Âm: h: là âm xát vô thanh, chỉ cần thở hơi nhẹ ra qua khoang miệng, tránh gằn cổ hay phát âm quá nặng.

data.title: Bài 106: Âm u ngắn /ʊ/
data.transcript:
​👈 Click on the speaker icon to listen! Under "Step 1"
​Make the sound short and relaxed: uh.
​How to say this sound:
Relax your lips completely and open your mouth slightly.
Pronounce a quick, crisp sound between "u" and "ư", without pushing your lips forward: uh.

​Letter rules:
Look for "oo" followed by k, d, or t in words like Book, Good, and Foot.
Look for "u" in short words like Put, Full, Bush, Sugar, Butcher, and Cushion.
Look for "o" in words like Wolf, Woman, and Bosom.
Look for "ou" in modal verbs like Could, Should, and Would.
​Word examples and meanings:
Book: a written work printed on paper pages. (Quyển sách)
Cook: to prepare food by heating it. (Nấu ăn)
Look: to direct your eyes toward something. (Nhìn)
Took: held or accepted something in the past. (Đã cầm, đã lấy)
Good: high in quality or pleasing. (Tốt, hay)
Wood: the hard material that forms the trunk of a tree. (Gỗ)
Foot: the lower part of the leg below the ankle. (Bàn chân)
Put: to move something into a specific position. (Đặt, để)
Full: holding as much as possible. (Đầy, no)
Pull: to exert force on something to move it toward you. (Kéo)
Push: to exert force on something to move it away from you. (Đẩy)
Bush: a low plant with many small branches. (Bụi cây)
Bull: an adult male animal of the cattle family. (Con bò đực)
Sugar: a sweet substance obtained from plants. (Đường ăn)
Butcher: a person who cuts and sells meat. (Thợ mổ, người bán thịt)
Cushion: a soft bag filled with material used for sitting. (Tấm đệm)
Wolf: a wild carnivorous mammal of the dog family. (Con chó sói)
Woman: an adult female human being. (Người phụ nữ)
Could: used as the past tense of can. (Có thể)
Should: used to indicate duty or correctness. (Nên)
Would: used to indicate a future intention or wish. (Sẽ, muốn)

​Practice sentence:
The good cook put some sugar on the food and took a look at the book.

​Key tip:
Keep your lips completely relaxed. Do not push your lips forward like the long U sound. Note: "blood" and "flood" are exceptions and are NOT short U sounds.

data.title: Bài 108: Âm A Bẹt (sound /æ/)
data.transcript:
​👈 Click on the speaker icon to listen! Under "Step 1"
​Make the sound wide and clear: æ
​How to say this sound:
Open your mouth wide, lower your jaw, and stretch the corners of your lips slightly.
Press the tip of your tongue against your lower front teeth and pronounce a short, clear sound between "a" and "e": 
æ
​Letter rules:
Look for "a" in short single-syllable words between consonants like Cat, Map, and Hat.
Look for "a" before double consonants like Apple, Letter, and Happy.
Look for "a" in words ending with consonants like "ack", "amp", "ang", or "ank" like Black, Lamp, Bang, and Bank.

​Word examples and meanings:
Cat: a small domesticated carnivorous mammal. (Con mèo)
Map: a diagrammatic representation of an area of land. (Bản đồ)
Hat: a shaped covering for the head worn for warmth or fashion. (Cái mũ)
Man: an adult male human being. (Người đàn ông)
Bad: of poor quality or a low standard. (Xấu, tồi tệ)
Apple: a round fruit with red or green skin and firm flesh. (Quả táo)
Happy: feeling or showing pleasure or contentment. (Vui vẻ, hạnh phúc)
Family: a group of one or two parents and their children. (Gia đình)
Black: of the darkest color, like night. (Màu đen)
Lamp: a device for giving light. (Cây đèn)
Bank: a financial establishment that uses money. (Ngân hàng)
Stamp: a small adhesive piece of paper stuck to a letter. (Tem thư)
Action: the process of doing something. (Hành động)
Animal: a living organism that feeds on organic matter. (Động vật)

​Practice sentence:
The happy man put a black hat and a map in his bag.

​Key tip:
Open your mouth wide like you are going to say "a", but shape your lips slightly like "e" to create a short, crisp sound.

data.title: Bài 65: Câu mệnh lệnh & Let's
data.theory:
1. Mệnh lệnh: V0 đầu câu, không chủ ngữ: Open the door, please. Be careful! Don't touch that! Never lie to me again!
2. Let's + V0 = Rủ làm gì cùng nhau: Let's go! Let's have lunch together. Let's not argue (phủ định).
3. Mệnh lệnh lịch sự: Please + V0 / Could you + V0...? / Would you mind + V-ing...?
4. Be + adj: Be quiet! Be patient! Be careful!
5. Dùng trong hướng dẫn, công thức, biển báo: Mix the flour with water. Keep off the grass.
data.examples:
1. Please turn off the lights when you leave the room. Thanks!
   (Làm ơn tắt đèn khi rời phòng nhé. Cảm ơn!)
2. Don't forget to bring your ID card tomorrow. You will need it.
   (Đừng quên mang thẻ căn cước ngày mai. Bạn sẽ cần nó.)
3. Let's meet at 7 PM at the coffee shop near my house, shall we?
   (Mình gặp nhau lúc 7h tối ở quán cà phê gần nhà mình nhé?)
4. Be careful with that hot pan! You might burn yourself.
   (Cẩn thận với cái chảo nóng đó! Bạn có thể bị bỏng.)
5. Take two tablets twice a day after meals. (Hướng dẫn dùng thuốc)
   (Uống 2 viên 2 lần/ngày sau bữa ăn.)

data.title: Bài 161: Nguyên âm đôi /eɪ/ và Quy tắc "E câm" (Magic E)
data.transcript:
Âm: eɪ: a đọc chệch sang i.
Khởi đầu bằng âm /e/ rồi trượt mượt mà sang âm /ɪ/, môi hơi dẹt sang hai bên, kéo dài âm khoảng một giây.
Đánh vần ghép âm:
m - a - k - e: đọc là: Make /meɪk/
c - a - k - e: đọc là: Cake /keɪk/
f - a - m - e: đọc là: Fame /feɪm/
l - a - t - e: đọc là: Late /leɪt/
r - a - i - n: đọc là: Rain /reɪn/
d - a - y: đọc là: Day /deɪ/
e - i - g - h - t: đọc là: Eight /eɪt/
Từ vựng và ý nghĩa:
Make: Làm, tạo ra. Cake: Bánh ngọt.
Fame: Sự nổi tiếng. Late: Muộn, trễ
Rain: Mưa. 
Day: Ngày. Eight: Số tám
Câu thực hành: They make eight cakes late on a rainy day for fame.
Lưu ý: Quy tắc Magic E: Khi từ có tận cùng là chữ e câm, nó sẽ làm nguyên âm đứng trước đọc thành tên của chính nó (âm đọc kéo dài như chữ cái trong bảng chữ cái, ví dụ: mat thành mate). Các mặt chữ phổ biến: a_e, ai, ay, ey, eigh.

data.title: Bài 80: Conversation Buying Meat for Dinner ✓ TuanQK English 🏪
data.transcript: Lisa went to a big supermarket to buy groceries. She decided to practice English by reading all the labels. She learned words like organic, meat expired, and discount. At the vegetable section, she tried to ask in English, Excuse me, where can I find basil? The staff did not understand, so she showed a picture on her phone. She found the basil. At the checkout, the cashier said, Do you need a bag? Lisa said, Yes, please. She paid and said, Thank you. Have a nice day. It was a small conversation, but she felt proud. She realized a supermarket is a great place to learn English because you see words everywhere. She created a listening lesson called Supermarket English with phrases like How much is this, Is there any discount, and Where is the dairy section. She tells students, You don't need to go to an English speaking country. You can practice in your local supermarket. Read labels, ask questions, and talk to cashiers. Every shopping trip is an English lesson if you want it to be.

Môi hơi chu ra phía trước, đầu lưỡi cong ngược lên về phía vòm miệng nhưng tuyệt đối không chạm vào vòm miệng, đẩy luồng hơi ra đồng thời làm rung dây thanh quản.
​Đánh vần ghép âm:
R - e - d: đọc là: Red /red/
R - i - g - h - t: đọc là: Right /raɪt/
C - a - r: đọc là: Car /kɑːr/
V - e - r - y: đọc là: Very /ˈveri/
S - o - r - r - y: đọc là: Sorry /ˈsɒri/.
​Từ vựng và ý nghĩa:
Red: Màu đỏ.
Right: Đúng, bên phải.
Car: Xe ô tô.
Very: Rất.
Sorry: Xin lỗi.
​Câu thực hành: The red car is very right, sorry.
​Lưu ý: Âm: r: là âm tiếp cận hữu thanh, giữ đầu lưỡi cong thả lỏng không chạm vòm họng, tránh rung đầu lưỡi như âm r trong tiếng Việt.

data.title: Bài 115: Các đoạn hội thoại - Thực hành hỏi và chỉ đường
data.transcript:
Conversations - Asking & Giving Directions Practices

​1. For Traveler & Passerby

​Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the central train station?

​Is there a post office or a bank near here?

​Am I heading in the right direction for the city museum?

​How far is it from here to the main square on foot?

​Is it within walking distance, or should I take a bus or taxi?

​Which bus line goes directly to the international airport?

​Where is the nearest subway station or bus stop?

​Could you show me where I am on this map?

​Do I need to turn left or turn right at the next intersection?

​Is the pharmacy on this street or around the block?

​How long does it take to walk to the shopping center from here?

​Can you point me towards the main entrance of the park?

​Where can I find a taxi stand around this area?

​Is there a landmark I should look for along the way?

​I seem to be lost. Can you help me find my hotel?

​2. Local Resident & Guide

​Go straight down this street for about two blocks.

​Turn left at the traffic lights and keep walking straight.

​Take the second turn on your right after the bridge.

​Walk past the supermarket, and you will see it on your left.

​It is right across from the library, next to the coffee shop.

​You are going the wrong way; you need to turn back.

​Follow this road until you reach the roundabout, then take the first exit.

​It is about a ten-minute walk from here.

​You can’t miss it; it is a large red building on the corner.

​Cross the street at the pedestrian crossing over there.

​Keep going until you hit the end of the avenue.

​It is located right behind the main shopping mall.

​Take bus number fifteen and get off at the third stop.

​It is a bit too far to walk, so I recommend taking a taxi.

​Just go straight ahead until you see the cathedral in front of you.

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: ASKING FOR A LANDMARK

​Traveler: "Excuse me, I am trying to find the national art gallery. Do you know where it is?"

​Resident: "Yes, I do. It is not too far from here. Are you walking or driving?"

​Traveler: "I am walking. How many minutes will it take to get there?"

​Resident: "It takes about ten minutes. Walk straight down this street until you hit the main intersection with the traffic lights."

​Traveler: "Okay, straight down to the traffic lights. Do I turn left or right there?"

​Resident: "Turn right at the traffic lights onto Central Avenue. Continue walking past a large park on your left."

​Traveler: "Turn right onto Central Avenue, past the park... Got it."

​Resident: "After the park, cross the street at the pedestrian zebra crossing. The gallery is the grand stone building right on the corner."

​Traveler: "That sounds very clear and easy to find. Thank you so much for your help!"

​Resident: "You are very welcome. Enjoy your visit!"

data.title: Bài 66: Too & Enough - Quá & Đủ
data.theory:
1. Too + adj/adv + to V = quá... đến nỗi KHÔNG thể (tiêu cực): Too expensive to buy (quá đắt nên không thể mua)
2. Adj/Adv + enough + to V = đủ... để có thể (tích cực): Old enough to drive (đủ tuổi để lái xe)
3. Enough + N + to V = đủ N để: I have enough money to buy it.
4. Too many + N đếm được, Too much + N không đếm được (quá nhiều): Too many cars, Too much traffic.
5. Phân biệt: too (quá, tiêu cực) vs very (rất, trung tính): This is too expensive = đắt quá (không mua được) vs This is very expensive = rất đắt (nhưng vẫn có thể mua).
data.examples:
1. This bag is too expensive. I can't afford it.
   (Túi này quá đắt. Tôi không mua nổi - too = không thể)
2. She is old enough to live by herself. She is 20 now.
   (Cô ấy đủ tuổi để sống một mình. Cô ấy 20 tuổi rồi - enough = có thể)
3. Do we have enough chairs for all the guests? Let's count again.
   (Chúng ta có đủ ghế cho tất cả khách không? Đếm lại nhé.)
4. There are too many advertisements on this website. It's annoying.
   (Có quá nhiều quảng cáo trên trang web này. Thật khó chịu.)
5. He speaks too quickly. I can't understand him at all.
   (Anh ấy nói quá nhanh. Tôi không hiểu gì cả.)

data.title: Bài 162: Cùng là ear nhưng khi đọc ơ và khi đọc ɪə
data.transcript:
Cùng mặt chữ "ear" nhưng có hai cách đọc chính rất phổ biến: âm /ɪə/ (ear) và âm /ɜː/ (ơ dài). Khi đọc /ɪə/, phát âm trượt nhẹ từ i sang ơ. Khi đọc /ɜː/, thả lỏng môi và giữ hơi dài âm ơ trong 1 giây.
Đánh vần ghép âm:
n - ear: đọc là: Near /nɪə/
h - ear: đọc là: Hear /hɪə/
c - l - ear: đọc là: Clear /klɪə/
l - ear - n: đọc là: Learn /lɜːn/
e - ar - t - h: đọc là: Earth /ɜːθ/
e - ar - l - y: đọc là: Early /ˈɜːli/
Vocabulary Examples:
Near: (Gần)
Hear: (Nghe)
Clear: (Rõ ràng)
Learn: (Học tập)
Earth: (Trái đất)
Early: (Sớm)
Practice Sentences: 
We hear clear sounds when we learn early on earth.
Notes: Đa số từ chứa "ear" đứng riêng hoặc ở cuối từ sẽ đọc là /ɪə/ (near, hear, clear, fear).
Khi "ear" đi trước một phụ âm (như n, th, l) thì thường chuyển sang đọc là /ɜː/ (learn, earth, early, earn).
Ngoại lệ cần chú ý: Một vài từ đặc biệt đọc là /eə/ như: bear, wear, pear.

👈 Click on the speaker icon to listen! Under "Step 1"
                 
     Make the sound long for one second: ee.
1. How to say this sound:
Smile wide and stretch your lips. 
Make the sound long for one second: /iː/ -> "ee".

2. Letter rules:
Look for "ee" in words like See, Green, and Three.
Look for "ea" in words like Tea, Eat, and Team.
Look for "ie" in words like Piece and Believe.

3. Word examples and meanings:
See: to look with your eyes. (Nhìn)
Tea: a hot drink. (Trà)
Eat: to take in food. (Ăn)

Piece: a part of something. (Miếng) 
Believe: to feel that something is true. (Tin tưởng)

4. Practice sentence:
I see a cup of green tea on the team table.

5. Key tip:
Keep the long E sound twice as long as the short I sound.

data.title: Bài 109: IELTS trong số  từ quen, những nghĩa  lạ.
data.transcript:
IELTS trong số  từ quen, những nghĩa  lạ này nha

Address (n, v) /əˈdres/
Nghĩa quen (n): địa chỉ
Nghĩa khác (v): giải quyết, xử lý
→ Governments should address environmental issues.
(Các chính phủ nên giải quyết những vấn đề môi trường.)

Subject (n, adj, v) /ˈsʌbdʒɪkt/ (n, adj); /səbˈdʒekt/ (v)
Nghĩa quen (n): môn học, chủ đề
Nghĩa khác (v): khiến ai/cái gì phải chịu một điều gì
→ Children are often subjected to intense academic pressure.
(Trẻ em thường phải chịu áp lực học tập lớn.)

Figure (n, v) /ˈfɪɡə(r)/
Nghĩa quen (n): con số, hình vẽ
Nghĩa khác (v): cho rằng, nghĩ rằng
→ I figured that the job would be more challenging.
(Tôi nghĩ rằng công việc đó sẽ khó khăn hơn.)

Issue (n, v) /ˈɪʃuː/
Nghĩa quen (n): vấn đề
Nghĩa khác (v): ban hành, phát hành
→ The government issued a new set of guidelines.
(Chính phủ đã ban hành bộ hướng dẫn mới.)

Fine (adj, n, v) /faɪn/
Nghĩa quen (adj): tốt, ổn; (n): tiền phạt
Nghĩa khác (v): phạt tiền; (adj): nhỏ mịn, tinh tế
→ Drivers can be fined for using their phones while driving.
(Người lái xe có thể bị phạt tiền vì sử dụng điện thoại khi lái xe.)

Capital (n, adj) /ˈkæpɪtl/
Nghĩa quen (n): thủ đô
Nghĩa khác (n): vốn
→ Small businesses often struggle to raise enough capital.
(Các doanh nghiệp nhỏ thường gặp khó khăn trong việc huy động đủ vốn.)

Mean (v, adj) /miːn/
Nghĩa quen (v): có nghĩa là; (adj): keo kiệt
Nghĩa khác (v): có ý định
→ I didn't mean to offend anyone.
(Tôi không có ý xúc phạm bất kỳ ai.)

Bear (n, v) /beə(r)/
Nghĩa quen (n): con gấu
Nghĩa khác (v): chịu đựng, gánh chịu
→ Many families cannot bear the rising cost of living.
(Nhiều gia đình không thể chịu nổi chi phí sinh hoạt ngày càng tăng.)

Sound (n, v, adj) /saʊnd/
Nghĩa quen (n): âm thanh
Nghĩa khác (adj): hợp lý, vững chắc
→ The proposal is based on sound reasoning.
(Đề xuất này dựa trên lập luận hợp lý.)

Fine (adj, n, v) /faɪn/
Nghĩa quen (adj): tốt, ổn; (n): tiền phạt
Nghĩa khác (adj): tinh tế, nhỏ mịn
→ The artist is known for her fine attention to detail.
(Nghệ sĩ này nổi tiếng với sự chú ý tỉ mỉ đến từng chi tiết.)

data.title: Bài 105: Âm u dài /uː/"oo" + L / M / N / P / T -> thường là U dài, nhóm ue, ew (cuối từ), ui, ou (đứng giữa), o, u (đứng 1 mình)
data.transcript:
​👈 Click on the speaker icon to listen! Under "Step 1"
 
​Make the sound long and smooth: oo.
​How to say this sound:
Round your lips tightly into a small circle and push them forward.
Keep the sound long and smooth for one second: oo.

​Letter rules:
Look for "oo" followed by l, m, n, p, or t in words like Cool, Room, Soon, Loop, and Boot.
Look for "u" standing alone in words like Rule, June, and Rude.
Look for "ew" at the end of words like New, Grew, and Flew.
Look for "ue" at the end of words like Blue, True, and Clue.
Look for "ui" in the middle of words like Fruit, Juice, and Suit.
Look for "ou" in the middle of words like Soup, Group, and Route.
Look for "o" standing alone in words like Do, To, and Who.

​Word examples and meanings:
Cool: moderately cold or chilling. (Mát mẻ)
Room: a space inside a building with walls. (Căn phòng)
Soon: in a short time from now. (Sớm)
Loop: a shape produced by a curve that crosses itself. (Vòng lặp)
Boot: a sturdy type of shoe covering the foot and ankle. (Đôi ủng, giày cao cổ)
Food: things that people and animals eat. (Thức ăn)
Moon: the round object that shines in the sky at night. (Mặt trăng)
Spoon: a tool used for eating soup or ice cream. (Cái thìa)
Rule: an official instruction about what you can or cannot do. (Quy tắc)
June: the sixth month of the year. (Tháng sáu)
Rude: not polite to other people. (Bất lịch sự)
New: not old or existing before. (Mới)
Grew: became bigger or larger. (Đã phát triển)
Flew: moved through the air like a bird. (Đã bay)
Blue: the color of the clear sky. (Màu xanh dương)
True: connected with facts or reality. (Sự thật)
Clue: a piece of information that helps solve a puzzle. (Manh mối)
Fruit: apples, bananas, and oranges. (Trái cây)
Juice: the liquid that comes from fruit or vegetables. (Nước ép)
Suit: a set of clothes made of the same fabric. (Bộ âu phục)
Soup: a liquid food made by cooking meat or vegetables. (Món súp, canh)
Group: a number of people or things located together. (Nhóm)
Route: a way or course taken in getting to a destination. (Tuyến đường)
Do: to perform an action or task. (Làm)
To: moving toward a place. (Đến)
Who: used to ask about a person. (Ai)

​Practice sentence:
The group enjoys hot soup and fresh fruit in the cool room.

​Key tip:
Keep your lips tightly rounded like you are blowing out a candle, and hold the sound longer than the short U sound.

data.title: Bài 107: Âm E Ngắn (Short E sound /e/) bổ sung đầy đủ trường hợp đặc biệt mặt chữ "ea" đọc thành /e/
data.transcript:
​👈 Click on the speaker icon to listen! Under "Step 1"
​Make the sound short and clear: eh.
​How to say this sound:
Open your mouth moderately and relax your lips.
Pronounce a short, clear sound without holding it long: eh.

​Letter rules:
Look for "e" in short single-syllable words like Bed, Pen, Ten, and Desk.
Look for "ea" before consonants like d, th, th-l, l-th, or th-r in words like Bread, Head, Dead, Heavy, Health, Weather, and Wealth.
Look for "a" in certain special words like Any and Many.

​Word examples and meanings:
Bed: a piece of furniture for sleep. (Cái giường)
Pen: a tool used for writing with ink. (Cây bút)
Ten: the number after nine. (Số mười)
Desk: a table used for studying or working. (Bàn làm việc)
Leg: one of the limbs used for walking. (Cái chân)
Help: to make it easier for someone to do something. (Giúp đỡ)
Bread: a food made from flour and water. (Bánh mì)
Head: the top part of the human body. (Cái đầu)
Dead: no longer alive. (Đã chết)
Heavy: weighing a lot. (Nặng)
Health: the state of being free from illness. (Sức khỏe)
Weather: the conditions outdoors like sunny or rainy. (Thời tiết)
Wealth: a large amount of money or valuable possessions. (Sự giàu có)
Ready: fully prepared for an action. (Sẵn sàng)
Sweater: a knitted garment worn on the upper body. (Áo len)
Threat: a statement of an intention to inflict pain or trouble. (Mối đe dọa)
Breath: the air taken into and let out of the lungs. (Hơi thở)
Any: one, some, or all of a number of things. (Bất kỳ)
Many: a large number of people or things. (Nhiều)
​Practice sentence:
He eats fresh bread for breakfast and gets ready in heavy weather.

​Key tip:
Remember that "ea" is not always a long "ee" sound. In words like bread, head, and weather, "ea" is pronounced as a short "eh" sound.

​You can claim your luggage at carousel number three downstairs.

​Please fill out this form at the lost luggage counter for assistance.

​Do you have anything to declare to customs today, sir?

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: CHECK-IN DESK & FLIGHT INQUIRIES

​Passenger: "Good morning. I would like to check in for my flight to Paris, please."

​Agent: "Good morning. May I see your passport and booking confirmation, please?"

​Passenger: "Here you go. Can I get a window seat near the front of the aircraft?"

​Agent: "Let me check... Yes, row 8 seat A is available. Do you have any checked baggage?"

​Passenger: "Just this one suitcase. Is there any delay on this flight today?"

​Agent: "No, sir. Everything is on schedule. Please put your bag on the scale."

​Passenger: "Great. Where is the security gate for international departures?"

​Agent: "Go straight up the escalator and turn right. Boarding starts at Gate B2 at 10:15."

​Passenger: "Thank you very much for your help."

​Agent: "You are very welcome. Have a pleasant flight!"

data.title: Bài 112: Các cuộc hội thoại - Bệnh viện & Cơ sở y tế
data.transcript:
Conversations - Hospital & Medical Practices

​1. For Patient & Visitor

​I would like to make an appointment with a general practitioner.

​Where is the emergency department located in this hospital?

​I have been feeling severe pain in my stomach since last night.

​Is there a specialist in cardiology available today?

​How long is the estimated waiting time to see the doctor?

​I have a history of high blood pressure and diabetes.

​I am allergic to penicillin and certain types of antibiotics.

​Could you please explain the potential side effects of this medication?

​How often should I take this medicine, and should I take it with food?

​Do I need to fast before taking this blood test tomorrow morning?

​Where can I get my prescription filled near the main clinic?

​Is this medical treatment covered by international health insurance?

​Could I get a copy of my medical report and test results?

​Where is the outpatient registration counter for new patients?

​Could you direct me to the radiology department for an X-ray?

​Can I schedule a follow-up appointment for next Tuesday?

​Are visiting hours restricted in the intensive care unit?

​I need a doctor's certificate for my sick leave at work.

​What should I do if my symptoms get worse over the weekend?

​Is there an interpreter available to help with translation?

​2. Medical Staff & Receptionist

​Please fill out this medical history form while you wait.

​May I please see your ID card and health insurance card?

​The doctor will call your name when it is your turn.

​Let me take your temperature, pulse, and blood pressure first.

​Please step onto the scale so I can check your weight.

​Where exactly do you feel the pain, and how long has it lasted?

​On a scale from one to ten, how severe is your pain right now?

​The doctor has ordered a blood test and a chest X-ray for you.

​Please roll up your sleeve so I can draw a sample of your blood.

​Take a deep breath in through your nose and hold it for three seconds.

​You need to take one tablet twice a day after meals.

​Make sure you complete the full course of antibiotics prescribed.

​Please rest as much as possible and drink plenty of fluids.

​We will receive your laboratory test results by tomorrow afternoon.

​If you experience any chest pain or breathing difficulty, return to the hospital immediately.

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: CONSULTATION & DIAGNOSIS

​Patient: "Good morning, doctor. I have had a severe headache and a high fever for three days."

​Doctor: "Good morning. Let me examine you. Do you have any other symptoms like a sore throat or body aches?"

​Patient: "Yes, my whole body feels sore, and I feel very tired all the time."

​Doctor: "I will check your temperature and blood pressure first... Your temperature is quite high at 38.5 degrees Celsius."

​Patient: "Is it something serious? Should I be worried?"

​Doctor: "It looks like a viral infection, but I want to run a quick blood test to be sure."

​Patient: "Okay, doctor. How long will it take to get the results?"

​Doctor: "About thirty minutes. While we wait, I will write you a prescription to help reduce your fever and relieve the pain."

​Patient: "Thank you, doctor. How should I take the medicine?"

​Doctor: "Take one pill every eight hours after eating, and make sure you rest and drink plenty of water."

data.title: Bài 113: Các cuộc hội thoại - Thực hành phỏng vấn xin việc
data.transcript:
Conversations - Job Interview Practices

​1. For Candidate (Applicant)

​Thank you for giving me the opportunity to interview for this position today.

​Could you tell me more about the daily responsibilities of this role?

​I have over five years of experience in software development and project management.

​In my previous role, I was responsible for leading a team of five developers.

​I am looking for a new challenge where I can grow my technical skills.

​One of my greatest strengths is my ability to solve complex problems under pressure.

​I am a quick learner and I adapt easily to new environments and technologies.

​Could you describe the ideal candidate you are looking for to fill this role?

​How does your team handle tight deadlines and high-priority project tasks?

​I am used to working in fast-paced environments with strict deadlines.

​My background in system design aligns very well with your project requirements.

​What are the biggest challenges facing the department at the moment?

​Are there opportunities for professional development and training within the company?

​I successfully improved our application performance by forty percent in my last project.

​How do you evaluate employee performance and measure success in this position?

​What is the company culture like, and how does the team collaborate?

​I am confident that my skills and experience make me a great fit for your team.

​What are the next steps in the hiring process, and when can I expect to hear back?

​2. Interviewer (Hiring Manager / HR)

​Welcome to our office. Thank you for taking the time to meet with us today.

​To start off, could you please introduce yourself and walk us through your resume?

​Why are you interested in joining our company for this specific position?

​What attracted you to this role, and why do you think you are a good fit?

​Can you describe a challenging situation at work and how you handled it?

​How do you prioritize your daily tasks when managing multiple urgent projects?

​What would you consider to be your greatest professional achievement so far?

​Where do you see yourself professionally in the next three to five years?

​How do you handle constructive criticism or feedback from team members?

​Could you give an example of a time when you had a disagreement with a colleague?

​What is your expected salary range for this position?

​How soon would you be able to start if you were offered the position?

​Do you prefer working independently or as part of a collaborative team?

​How do you stay updated with the latest industry trends and technologies?

​Do you have any questions for us regarding the position or the company?

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: JOB INTERVIEW & PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

​Interviewer: "Good morning. It is a pleasure to meet you. Did you find our office easily today?"

​Candidate: "Good morning. It is a pleasure to meet you too. Yes, the directions were very clear and I arrived with plenty of time."

​Interviewer: "Great! To begin, could you please give us a brief introduction of yourself and your professional background?"

​Candidate: "Certainly. I have been working as a mobile app developer for the past four years. During this time, I specialized in building Kotlin applications and designing efficient user interfaces."

​Interviewer: "That sounds impressive. What made you decide to apply for this position at our company?"

​Candidate: "I have been following your company’s projects for a while. I admire your innovative products, and I believe my background in mobile development aligns perfectly with your goals."

​Interviewer: "Can you tell me about a major project you completed recently and your role in it?"

​Candidate: "In my last project, I led the development of a real-time data tracking app. I was responsible for system architecture, database management, and optimizing overall performance."

​Interviewer: "Excellent. How do you handle tight deadlines when unexpected issues arise?"

​Candidate: "I prioritize tasks by urgency and impact, communicate immediately with the team, and focus on delivering a stable core solution before refining additional features."

​Interviewer: "Thank you for sharing that. Do you have any questions for us about the role or our team?"

​Candidate: "Yes, I would love to know more about the team structure and the primary goals for this position over the next six months."

data.title: Bài 114: Các cuộc hội thoại - Thực tiễn tại nhà hàng
data.transcript:
Conversations - Restaurant Practices

​1. For Guest (Customer)

​Do you have a table available for two people for this evening?

​Could we please get a table near the window or on the terrace?

​We have a reservation under the name Pham for seven o'clock.

​Could we see the lunch menu and the wine list, please?

​What do you recommend as the house specialty for dinner today?

​Are there any vegetarian or gluten-free options on the menu?

​Is this dish spicy, and can we request it to be made mild?

​Does this seafood dish contain any nuts or dairy products?

​We are ready to order now. Could you please take our order?

​I would like the grilled steak, medium-rare, with a side salad.

​Could we get a bottle of sparkling water and two glasses of orange juice?

​Could you bring us some extra napkins and an extra set of cutlery?

​Excuse me, we have been waiting for over thirty minutes for our food.

​I ordered the fried chicken, but I was brought the grilled fish instead.

​Could you please warm this soup up a bit more? It is a little cold.

​Everything was absolutely delicious. Compliments to the chef!

​Could we see the dessert menu before you clear the table?

​We would like to pay the bill now. Do you accept credit cards?

​Could you please split the bill evenly between two cards?

​Is the service charge already included in the final bill?

​2. Restaurant Staff & Waiter

​Good evening! Welcome to our restaurant. Do you have a reservation?

​Right this way, please. Let me show you to your table.

​Here are your menus. I will be back in a few minutes to take your order.

​Are you ready to order, or would you like a few more minutes?

​Would you like to start with some appetizers or drinks first?

​How would you like your steak cooked: rare, medium, or well-done?

​Would you like fries or mashed potatoes with your main course?

​I am sorry, but we are completely out of the fresh salmon tonight.

​Our daily special is fresh seafood pasta served with a white wine sauce.

​Please be careful, the plate is extremely hot!

​Is everything to your satisfaction with the food so far?

​May I clear these empty plates and glasses for you?

​Would you like to see our dessert menu or order some coffee?

​Your total comes to eighty-five dollars. How would you like to pay?

​Thank you very much for dining with us! Have a wonderful evening!

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: ORDERING FOOD & DINING EXPERIENCE

​Waiter: "Good evening, sir. Welcome to our restaurant. How many people are in your party?"

​Guest: "Good evening. A table for two, please. We do not have a reservation."

​Waiter: "No problem at all. Please follow me, I have a lovely table available near the window."

​Guest: "Thank you. Could we please see the menu and get two glasses of water to start?"

​Waiter: "Certainly. Here are your menus and your water. Are you ready to order your main course, or do you need a few more minutes?"

​Guest: "We are ready. I will have the grilled salmon with roast vegetables, and my friend would like the beef sirloin steak."

​Waiter: "Excellent choice. How would your friend like the steak prepared?"

​Guest: "Medium-rare, please. Also, could we get the sauce on the side?"

​Waiter: "Of course. One grilled salmon and one medium-rare sirloin steak with sauce on the side. I will put that order in for you right away."

​Guest: "Thank you very much for your assistance!"

data.title: Bài 116: Các đoạn hội thoại - Thực hành đi trên xe Taxi
data.transcript:
Conversations - Taking a Taxi Practices

​1. For Passenger

​Excuse me, are you available, or is this taxi taken?

​Could you please take me to this address on my phone?

​How much will it cost to get to the international airport?

​Are you going to use the meter, or is it a flat rate?

​How long will it take to get to the city center at this hour?

​Could you please put my heavy suitcases in the trunk?

​Is the traffic heavy on the main highway right now?

​Could you please turn on the air conditioning a little bit?

​Could you please roll up the window? It is quite noisy outside.

​Can you slow down a bit, please? I am not in a hurry.

​Could you drive a little faster, please? My flight leaves soon.

​Is it faster to take the toll road or the local street?

​Do I need to pay extra for the highway toll fee?

​Can you stop near the convenience store over there for a minute?

​Could you please drop me off right in front of the hotel entrance?

​You can pull over right here on the right side of the street.

​Do you accept credit card payments, or is it cash only?

​Do you have change for a fifty-dollar bill?

​Could you give me a printed receipt for this trip, please?

​Keep the change! Thank you for the safe ride.

​2. Taxi Driver

​Hello! Where would you like to go today?

​Do you have any luggage that needs to go in the trunk?

​I will turn on the taximeter now. The starting fare is three dollars.

​The total fare to the airport is fixed at thirty-five dollars.

​Traffic is very heavy during peak hours, so it might take forty minutes.

​Which route would you prefer: the highway or the inner city roads?

​There is a two-dollar toll fee for using the express bridge.

​Please fasten your seatbelt for safety during the trip.

​We are almost there. It is just around the corner ahead.

​Where exactly would you like me to stop or pull over?

​Your total fare comes to twenty-two dollars on the meter.

​Would you like to pay with cash, card, or via the mobile app?

​Here is your change and your receipt. Check your belongings before getting out.

​Watch out for oncoming motorcycles when you open the car door!

​Thank you for riding with me. Have a great day!

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: CATCHING A TAXI TO THE TRAIN STATION

​Passenger: "Hello! Are you free? Can you take me to the central train station?"

​Driver: "Hello! Yes, jump in. I will put your bags in the trunk for you."

​Passenger: "Thank you very much. How long will it take to get there?"

​Driver: "It usually takes about fifteen minutes, but the morning traffic is a bit slow today. It might take around twenty-five minutes."

​Passenger: "I see. My train leaves in forty minutes, so please take the quickest route."

​Driver: "No problem at all. I will take the expressway to avoid the crowded downtown streets."

​Passenger: "Great. Will you be using the meter?"

​Driver: "Yes, the meter is running. The base fare starts at three dollars."

​(Arriving at the destination)

​Driver: "Here we are, right in front of the main entrance to the station. The meter shows eighteen dollars."

​Passenger: "Perfect. Can I pay with a credit card?"

​Driver: "Yes, card payments are accepted. Just tap your card on the reader here."

​Passenger: "There you go. Could I also get a receipt, please?"

​Driver: "Here is your receipt. Let me get your luggage out of the trunk. Have a safe journey!"

data.transcript:
Conversations - Bus & Subway Practices

​1. For Passenger

​Which bus line goes directly to the city center?

​Does this subway train stop at the central square station?

​How much is a single ride ticket to the national museum?

​Where can I buy a reloadable transit card or a day pass?

​Is this seat reserved for elderly, pregnant, or disabled passengers?

​How many stops are there until the international terminal?

​Which line do I need to transfer to for the central station?

​Where is the transfer station between the blue line and the red line?

​Could you please tell me when we reach the next stop?

​Do I need to tap my card again when exiting the station?

​Is this the express train or the local train that stops everywhere?

​Which platform does the westbound train depart from?

​Is there a subway map available in English inside the station?

​Excuse me, I am getting off at the next stop. Could I squeeze past?

​Mind the gap between the train platform and the doors!

​Is this seat taken, or may I sit here?

​What time does the last train run tonight?

​Are bicycles allowed on the train during peak hours?

​Which exit should I take for the shopping street?

​Is Wi-Fi connection available on board this bus?

​2. Bus Driver & Transit Staff

​Please step inside and move towards the back of the bus.

​Please have your ticket, pass, or contactless card ready to scan.

​This bus does not accept cash payments; you must use a transit card.

​The fare is two dollars and fifty cents for a single journey.

​Please validate your ticket at the yellow machine near the door.

​Next stop is the Central Public Library. Doors open on the right.

​This train terminates at the current station. All passengers must exit.

​Please stand clear of the sliding doors as they are closing.

​Please offer this seat to elderly passengers or people in need.

​To reach line two, follow the green arrows down the escalator.

​You need to take platform four on the lower level for northbound trains.

​Please keep your personal belongings with you at all times.

​Hold on tightly to the handrails while the vehicle is moving.

​Press the stop button in advance if you wish to alight at the next stop.

​The next station is the Airport Terminal; transfers available for line five.

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: TAKING THE SUBWAY & TRANSFERRING LINES

​Passenger: "Excuse me, I am trying to get to the Art Museum. Does this train go there?"

​Staff: "No, this is line one. You need to take line three to reach the museum station."

​Passenger: "I see. Where can I transfer from line one to line three?"

​Staff: "Stay on this train for three more stops and get off at City Hall station. That is the main interchange."

​Passenger: "Okay, get off at City Hall station. Which platform do I go to for line three?"

​Staff: "Once you exit the train, follow the blue overhead signs for line three towards the northbound platform."

​Passenger: "Great. Do I need to tap my card and pay an extra fare when transferring?"

​Staff: "No, as long as you remain inside the fare gates, the transfer is completely free."

​Passenger: "Thank you very much! How often do the trains run on line three?"

​Staff: "They run every four to five minutes during the day, so you won't have to wait long."

data.title: Bài 28: Âm /v/ (v hữu thanh)
data.transcript:
Hướng dẫn khẩu hình: v: hữu thanh.
Khẩu hình giống âm f, răng cửa trên chạm nhẹ vào môi dưới rồi đẩy hơi xát ra nhưng làm rung dây thanh quản.
​Đánh vần ghép âm:
V - e - r - y: đọc là: Very /ˈveri/
L - o_e - v: đọc là: Love /lʌv/
V - oi - ce: đọc là: Voice /vɔɪs/
H - a_e - v: đọc là: Have /hæv/
M - o_e - v: đọc là: Move /muːv/.
​Từ vựng và ý nghĩa:
Very: Rất.
Love: Yêu.
Voice: Giọng nói.
Have: Có.
Move: Di chuyển.
​Câu thực hành: I very love your voice and have to move.
​Lưu ý: Âm: v: là âm xát hữu thanh, chú ý giữ răng chạm môi dưới và làm rung cổ họng khi phát âm.

data.title: Bài 118: Các cuộc hội thoại - Những thông lệ tại siêu thị
data.transcript:
Conversations - Supermarket Practices

​1. For Customer

​Excuse me, where can I find the fresh dairy products and milk?

​Which aisle are the canned vegetables and sauces located in?

​Do you have organic fruits and vegetables in stock today?

​Is this brand of olive oil currently on sale or discounted?

​Where can I find frozen seafood and ice cream?

​Do you have any gluten-free or sugar-free bread available?

​Could you please help me reach that box on the top shelf?

​Where are the shopping carts and hand baskets located?

​Is there a bakery section for freshly baked bread and pastries?

​Are these apples sold by weight or by individual piece?

​Where can I weigh these fresh vegetables to get a price label?

​Can I check the expiration date on this carton of juice?

​Do you have any fresh meat or seafood counters in the back?

​Where can I find household cleaning items and paper towels?

​Is the express checkout lane open for items under ten pieces?

​Do I need to pay extra for a plastic or paper shopping bag?

​Do you accept mobile app payments or contactless cards here?

​Can I return this unopened item if I keep the purchase receipt?

​Where is the customer service desk for item returns?

​Are there any buy-one-get-one-free promotions today?

​2. Cashier & Supermarket Staff

​Good day! Did you find everything you were looking for today?

​Please place all your items on the conveyor belt.

​Do you have a supermarket membership card or loyalty app to scan?

​Would you like to purchase a reusable shopping bag for your items?

​These items are part of our buy-one-get-one-free promotion today.

​You need to weigh your fresh fruit at the produce scale over there first.

​Your total purchase comes to forty-five dollars and fifty cents.

​How would you like to pay: with cash, credit card, or mobile pay?

​Please tap or insert your payment card into the card reader.

​Here is your receipt and your change. Thank you for shopping with us!

​Would you like your receipt placed inside the bag or handed to you?

​The express checkout lane is limited to ten items or fewer, sir.

​I am sorry, but this item is out of stock at the moment.

​Let me call another staff member to check the price of this item for you.

​Have a wonderful day and see you again soon!

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: CHECKOUT & STORE PROMOTIONS

​Customer: "Good afternoon! Could you tell me if this coffee package is on sale today?"

​Cashier: "Good afternoon! Let me scan it for you... Yes, it is currently twenty percent off."

​Customer: "That is great! Also, where can I find fresh eggs? I couldn't see them in aisle three."

​Cashier: "The fresh eggs are located in aisle six, right next to the dairy and milk section."

​Customer: "Thank you. I will quickly get a carton of eggs and bring it here."

​(Customer returns with the item)

​Cashier: "Alright, I have scanned all your items. Do you have our store loyalty card?"

​Customer: "Yes, I have the barcode on my phone. Let me bring it up... Here you go."

​Cashier: "Scanned! That earned you fifty reward points. Your total comes to thirty-two dollars."

​Customer: "Perfect. Can I pay with a contactless card?"

​Cashier: "Yes, just tap your card on the terminal... Payment successful! Here is your receipt."

data.title: Bài 119: Các cuộc trao đổi – Thực tiễn trong lớp học và giảng đường
data.transcript:
Conversations - Classroom & Lecture Hall Practices

​1. For Student

​Good morning, professor. May I come in, please?

​Excuse me, could you please repeat that last point again?

​Could you speak a little louder, please? It is hard to hear in the back.

​Which textbook chapter are we covering for today's lecture?

​Could you please explain this grammar rule with another example?

​Is this topic going to be included in the upcoming mid-term exam?

​What is the deadline for submitting our group project assignment?

​Are we allowed to use calculators or reference sheets during the test?

​Could you please write that key formula or term on the whiteboard?

​May I be excused for a few minutes to go to the restroom?

​I missed yesterday's class due to illness. May I borrow your lecture notes?

​Could you clarify the main requirements for the essay assignment?

​Where should we upload our homework files: on the portal or via email?

​Will the presentation slides be uploaded to the student portal later today?

​Can we form our own study groups, or will you assign the team members?

​Is there any office hour available this week for individual consultations?

​I didn't quite catch the homework instructions. Could you repeat them?

​Should our research paper follow APA or MLA citation format?

​Could you give us some guidance on how to structure our presentation?

​Thank you for your time and explanation, professor.

​2. Teacher & Professor

​Good morning, everyone! Please take your seats so we can begin.

​Has everyone submitted their individual assignment from last week?

​Please open your textbooks to page forty-five and read the first paragraph.

​Quiet down, please! Turn off your mobile phones or set them to silent mode.

​Today, we are going to cover the fundamental principles of system design.

​Does anyone have any questions regarding the topic we discussed last class?

​Please raise your hand if you would like to answer the question on the board.

​I would like you to split into groups of four for this discussion activity.

​Make sure you hand in your final papers before five PM on Friday.

​You will have thirty minutes to complete this pop quiz independently.

​Please pay close attention to this section; it will be on the final exam.

​Let's take a ten-minute break before we start the second half of the lecture.

​Don't forget to review chapter six before our next class on Thursday.

​That is all for today's lecture. Thank you for your active participation!

​If you need further help with your project, drop by my office during office hours.

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: ASKING QUESTIONS & ASSIGNMENT DETAILS

​Student: "Excuse me, professor. Do you have a moment after class?"

​Professor: "Sure! How can I help you today?"

​Student: "I was reviewing the project guidelines, and I had a question about the final presentation."

​Professor: "Of course. What specific part are you unsure about?"

​Student: "Does each team member need to speak during the presentation, or can one person present on behalf of the group?"

​Professor: "Every team member must present a section to receive individual grading for public speaking."

​Student: "I understand. Also, what is the maximum time limit for the presentation?"

​Professor: "Each group has fifteen minutes in total, followed by a five-minute Q&A session."

​Student: "Got it! Should we bring physical handouts, or just send you the digital slides?"

​Professor: "Just upload your presentation slides to the student portal before midnight the day before."

​Student: "That is very clear. Thank you so much for your time, professor!"

​Professor: "You are very welcome. Good luck with your preparation!"

Conversations - Office & Workplace Practices

​1. For Employee & Team Member

​Good morning! Could you please update me on the status of today's project?

​I have sent you the updated financial report via email for your review.

​Could we schedule a short sync-up meeting this afternoon at two o'clock?

​I am currently working on fixing the bug reported in the latest release.

​Could you please give me feedback on the draft proposal I submitted yesterday?

​I need to request two days of annual leave for next week.

​I will be working remotely from home tomorrow due to personal business.

​Who is leading the cross-departmental coordination for this project?

​Could you please share the access link to the shared Google Drive folder?

​I am running a bit behind schedule because of an unexpected technical issue.

​Let's discuss this task in detail during our weekly team stand-up.

​Could you forward me the email thread regarding the client's feedback?

​I am CC'ing the project manager on this email so everyone stays informed.

​What is the hard deadline for finalizing the quarterly budget plan?

​I will prepare the presentation slides for our client demonstration on Friday.

​Could you help me troubleshoot this issue with the internal server connection?

​The conference room on the third floor is already reserved for another team.

​I am taking my lunch break now and will be back at my desk by one PM.

​I will send out the meeting minutes and action items by the end of the day.

​Thank you for your assistance with this task; I really appreciate your support.

​2. Manager, Team Lead & HR

​Welcome to our team! Let me introduce you to your department colleagues.

​Please make sure to log your working hours in the time-tracking system daily.

​We need to align our department goals with the overall company strategy.

​Let's go around the table so everyone can share their progress updates.

​Great job on delivering the project ahead of the deadline!

​Could you please prioritize this urgent task before working on other items?

​We need to cut down on project costs to stay within our allocated budget.

​Please review the revised company policy document in the employee handbook.

​Let's set up a one-on-one performance review meeting for next Tuesday.

​Could you please delegate this responsibility to one of the junior developers?

​We are holding an all-hands staff meeting in the main auditorium at ten AM.

​Please ensure all client data is handled according to our security protocols.

​We need to hire two additional team members for the upcoming product expansion.

​I will approve your leave request in the system before the end of the day.

​Let's wrap up today's meeting and follow up on these points next Monday.

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: PROJECT DEADLINE & TEAM COLLABORATION

​Colleague A: "Hi! Do you have a few minutes to talk about the upcoming software release?"

​Colleague B: "Sure! I just finished reviewing the user interface design. What's up?"

​Colleague A: "Our client requested a few minor adjustments to the login page. Can we implement them by tomorrow?"

​Colleague B: "Tomorrow might be a bit tight since we are testing the backend API right now. When is the final deadline?"

Conversations - Factory & Workshop Practices

​1. For Worker & Technician

​Good morning! I am reporting for my shift on assembly line number two.

​Where can I find the personal protective equipment and safety goggles?

​Please make sure to wear your safety helmet and steel-toe boots at all times.

​The conveyor belt on line three is making an unusual noise and running slowly.

​I need to report a minor mechanical fault with the stamping machine.

​Could you please pass me the adjustable wrench and the screwdriver set?

​Has the raw material batch been inspected and approved by quality control?

​We need to restock the supply of bolts, screws, and washers in this work area.

​Please check the pressure gauge reading before turning on the main valve.

​Do not operate this machinery without verifying that the emergency stop switch works.

​We need to perform routine maintenance and lubrication on the robotic arm today.

​The production quota for this shift is five hundred units.

​Where is the chemical waste disposal area located in this facility?

​Is there a spare part for this hydraulic pump in the central warehouse?

​Please lock out and tag out the power source before starting any repair work.

​The temperature sensor reading is higher than the standard operating limit.

​We have successfully completed the quality check for the first batch of products.

​Please clean up your workstation and organize the tools before ending your shift.

​Where is the nearest eye wash station and first aid kit in this workshop?

​The inventory level of raw materials is getting low for tomorrow's production run.

​2. Supervisor, Engineer & Quality Control

​Welcome to the production floor. Please follow all safety guidelines carefully.

​Attention everyone, we will hold a quick five-minute stand-up meeting before starting the shift.

​Please double-check the calibration settings on the control panel before running the machine.

​Quality control reported a minor defect rate on the previous production batch.

​We need to halt the line immediately to investigate the cause of the defect.

​Please follow the standard operating procedure step by step to ensure product safety.

​Make sure all safety guards are properly installed before starting the equipment.

​We are adjusting the line speed to match the target output rate for this afternoon.

​Who was responsible for performing the routine inspection on machine number four?

​Please fill out the daily maintenance log sheet after completing your check.

​We need to conduct a safety audit on all electrical cabinets this afternoon.

​Please store all flammable materials in the designated fireproof storage cabinet.

​Heavy machinery is operating in this zone; please stay within the yellow walkways.

​We are implementing a new workflow process to improve overall production efficiency.

​Great effort everyone! We met our daily production target with zero safety incidents.

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: EQUIPMENT MAINTENANCE & LINE TROUBLESHOOTING

​Worker: "Excuse me, supervisor. Machine number three on line two just stopped working unexpectedly."

​Supervisor: "Did any warning lights or error codes appear on the control display?"

​Worker: "Yes, the red indicator light is flashing, and error code E-04 is showing on the panel."

​Supervisor: "Error E-04 usually indicates a motor overheating issue or a material jam in the feeder."

​Worker: "Should I try pressing the reset button to restart the machine?"

​Supervisor: "No, do not restart it yet. First, hit the emergency stop button and lock out the power supply."

​Worker: "Understood. I will disconnect the power and set up the safety maintenance sign."

​Supervisor: "Good. I will call the maintenance engineer to inspect the motor drive and clear the feeder mechanism."

​Worker: "How long do you think the repair will take? Should I help on line one in the meantime?"

​Supervisor: "Yes, please assist line one with packing while we resolve this issue. I will inform you as soon as line two is ready."

data.transcript:
Conversations - Auto Repair Shop & Garage Practices

​1. For Vehicle Owner & Customer

​Good morning! I brought my car in for a routine oil change and maintenance check.

​There is a strange squeaking sound whenever I press down on the brake pedal.

​The engine indicator light on my dashboard turned on while I was driving yesterday.

​My car is pulling slightly to the left side when I am driving on the highway.

​Could you please check the wheel alignment and balance all four tires?

​The air conditioning system is blowing warm air instead of cold air.

​I am experiencing a noticeable vibration in the steering wheel at high speeds.

​The battery seems weak because the engine is struggling to start in the morning.

​How much will it cost to replace the front brake pads and brake rotors?

​Could you inspect the suspension system and check the shock absorbers?

​How long will the diagnostic check and repairs take to finish?

​Please give me an estimated cost quote before starting any major repair work.

​Do you use original manufacturer spare parts or aftermarket replacement parts?

​Is the radiator leaking coolant, or is it just a loose rubber hose?

​I think there is an oil leak underneath the car because I noticed spots on the driveway.

​Could you also top up the windshield washer fluid and check the tire pressure?

​Is this repair covered under warranty, or will I need to pay out of pocket?

​Could you keep the replaced broken parts so I can see them when I pick up the car?

​What time can I come back to pick up my vehicle this afternoon?

​Can I pay the repair bill using a credit card or mobile bank transfer?

​2. Mechanic, Technician & Service Advisor

​Welcome to our auto repair shop! How can we assist you with your vehicle today?

​Please pop the hood so I can take a look at the engine bay.

​We will connect our diagnostic scanner to read the trouble codes from your car's ECU.

​The scan tool shows a misfire fault in cylinder number two.

​Your front brake pads are worn down to less than three millimeters and need replacement.

​The air filter and cabin filter are dirty and should be replaced during this service.

​We found a minor oil leak coming from the valve cover gasket.

​The alternator is not charging the battery properly, which is why your car won't start.

​We need to flush and replace the old transmission fluid and coolant.

​Your tires are unevenly worn, so we recommend a wheel alignment and tire rotation.

​It will take about two hours to complete the brake replacement and oil change.

​Here is the detailed cost estimate for the required parts and repair labor.

​We will call you immediately if we find any additional issues during the inspection.

​All our repair work and replaced parts come with a six-month warranty.

​Your car is fully serviced, road-tested, and ready for pickup at your convenience.

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: DIAGNOSING CAR PROBLEMS & REPAIR ESTIMATE

​Customer: "Good morning! I would like to have my car checked. The engine has been making a clicking noise when I accelerate."

​Mechanic: "Good morning! Let's take a look. Does the clicking sound get faster as you speed up?"

​Customer: "Yes, exactly. It gets louder and faster when I step on the gas pedal."

​Mechanic: "It could be a worn CV joint or an issue with the engine drive belt. Let me put your car on the lift and inspect it."

​Customer: "How long will the initial inspection take?"

​Mechanic: "Give us about thirty minutes. We will inspect the drive shafts, belts, and run a full diagnostic scan."

​(Thirty minutes later)

​Mechanic: "We found the cause of the noise. The outer boot on your front right CV joint is torn, causing the joint to lose grease and wear out."

​Customer: "I see. Does the whole axle assembly need to be replaced, or just the joint?"

​Mechanic: "Replacing the complete drive shaft assembly is safer and more cost-effective in the long run. I can have it fixed by four PM today."

​Customer: "Could you give me a written estimate for the total cost, including parts and labor?"

​Mechanic: "Certainly! Here is the cost breakdown. If you approve the estimate, we can start working on it right away."

data.title: Bài 57: Nuốt âm /h/ và rút gọn (Contractions and Weak Forms)
data.transcript:
1. Quy tắc: Trong nói nhanh, /h/ ở đầu đại từ (he, him, his, her) thường bị nuốt. Các dạng rút gọn phổ biến.
2. Ví dụ:
- Tell_him /tel_ɪm/ → /telɪm/ (bảo anh ấy)
- Ask_her /ɑːsk_ər/ → /ɑːskər/ (hỏi cô ấy)
- I have /aɪv/, You have /jʊv/, He is /hiːz/ → /ɪz/ trong câu nhanh
- Going to /ɡənə/ (gonna), Want to /wɒnə/ (wanna), Have to /hæftə/ (hafta)
- Do you /dʒə/ → /dʒə/ trong Do you want? /dʒəwɒnə/?
3. Câu thực hành: Tell him I wanna gonna have to ask her.
4. Lưu ý: Weak forms: to /tə/, for /fər/, and /ən/, of /əv/.

data.title: Bài 67: So & Such ... that - Quá ... đến nỗi
data.theory:
1. So + adj/adv + that + S+V = quá... đến nỗi mà: It was so hot that we stayed inside (Trời nóng quá đến nỗi chúng tôi ở trong nhà)
2. Such + (a/an) + adj + N + that + S+V = quá... đến nỗi: It was such a hot day that... (Đó là một ngày nóng quá đến nỗi...)
3. So much/many/little/few + N + that: There was so much traffic that we were late.
4. Phân biệt So vs Such: So + adj/adv, Such + N (có adj). So beautiful vs Such a beautiful girl.
5. Dùng trong IELTS Writing để nhấn mạnh kết quả.
data.examples:
1. The movie was so boring that I fell asleep after 20 minutes.
   (Phim chán quá đến nỗi tôi ngủ gật sau 20 phút.)
2. It was such a beautiful sunset that everyone stopped to take photos.
   (Hoàng hôn đẹp quá đến nỗi mọi người đều dừng lại chụp ảnh.)
3. There were so many people at the concert that we couldn't find a place to sit.
   (Có quá nhiều người ở buổi hòa nhạc đến nỗi chúng tôi không tìm được chỗ ngồi.)
4. He speaks so quickly that nobody can understand him.
   (Anh ấy nói nhanh quá đến nỗi không ai hiểu được.)
5. She is such a kind person that everyone loves her.
   (Cô ấy là người tốt bụng đến nỗi ai cũng yêu quý.)

data.transcript:
Conversations - Nail Salon Practices

​1. For Customer

​Good morning! I would like to book a manicure and a pedicure, please.

​Do you have any available appointments this afternoon around three o'clock?

​Can I get a basic gel manicure with a simple nail art design?

​Could I see your color chart and polish samples to pick a shade?

​I have an existing set of acrylic nails that need to be removed first.

​Could you please shape my nails into an oval or almond shape?

​I prefer my nails to be kept short and square with rounded edges.

​How much extra do you charge for custom hand-drawn nail designs?

​Could you please trim my cuticles gently? My skin is quite sensitive.

​I would like a classic French manicure with a subtle nude base.

​Do you offer dip powder or gel extension services here?

​Could you fix this chipped nail on my index finger, please?

​I brought a photo on my phone. Can you replicate this design?

​How long does a full set of gel extensions usually last?

​Could you please apply a top coat to make it extra shiny and long-lasting?

​I would like a relaxing foot massage along with my spa pedicure.

​Is the foot basin sanitized and disinfected after every customer?

​Could you please scrub off the calluses on the bottom of my feet?

​Do you have any non-toxic or vegan nail polish options?

​Can I pay the bill using a credit card or mobile bank transfer?

​2. Nail Technician & Salon Staff

​Welcome to our nail salon! Do you have an appointment with us today?

​Please pick a color from our swatch book while we prepare your station.

​Would you like gel polish, regular polish, or dip powder for your nails today?

​Please place your hands inside the UV LED lamp to cure the gel layer.

​Would you prefer your nails square, round, oval, almond, or coffin shape?

​Do you need your previous gel or acrylic set removed before we start?

​Please soak your feet in the warm foot bath while I prepare the tools.

​Our tools are fully sterilized and sealed in individual pouches for safety.

​Your cuticles are a bit dry; I will apply a hydrating cuticle oil for you.

​Please be careful not to touch your phone or keys while your nails are drying.

​How does the length and shape of this nail look to you so far?

​We have a special discount today if you get both a manicure and a pedicure.

​Would you like any glitter, rhinestones, or chrome powder effect added?

​Please let me know if the water in the foot bath is too hot or too cold.

​All finished! Your nails look absolutely beautiful. Have a wonderful day!

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: GETTING A GEL MANICURE & PEDICURE

​Technician: "Good afternoon! Welcome to our salon. What services are you looking to get today?"

​Customer: "Hi, good afternoon! I would like to get a gel manicure and a spa pedicure, please."

​Technician: "Wonderful! Do you need us to remove any old polish or acrylics first?"

​Customer: "Yes, I have some leftover gel polish on my fingernails that needs to be soaked off."

​Technician: "No problem at all. Please take a look at our color wheel and choose your shades while I start soaking off your old gel."

​Customer: "Thank you. I am looking for a soft pastel pink for my hands and a deep burgundy for my feet."

​Technician: "Great choices! What nail shape would you like for your manicure today?"

​Customer: "I would like an almond shape, but please don't make them too long."

​Technician: "Got it, short almond shape. Would you like any accent designs or rhinestones on your ring fingers?"

​Customer: "Just a simple white French tip on the ring fingers, please."

​Technician: "Perfect! Please place your foot in the warm spa bath, and we will begin with your pedicure first."

​Customer: "Sounds great, thank you!"

data.transcript:
Conversations - Hair Salon Practices

​1. For Customer

​Good morning! I would like to get a haircut and a wash, please.

​Do you have any openings for a walk-in, or do I need an appointment?

​I just want a light trim to get rid of the split ends.

​Could you take off about two inches from the length, please?

​I brought a picture on my phone to show you the style I want.

​Could you layer my hair a bit to give it more volume and texture?

​I would like to thin out my hair because it feels very thick and heavy.

​Could you please cut my bangs so they sit just above my eyebrows?

​How much do you charge for a full head hair coloring and highlights?

​I want to dye my hair a warm chocolate brown shade.

​Do I need to bleach my hair first to get this light ash blonde color?

​Could you recommend a hair treatment for dry and damaged hair?

​I would like to get a soft wave perm for a more natural look.

​Could you blow-dry and style my hair for a special event tonight?

​Please don't cut it too short on the top; just trim the sides.

​Could you use a low guard on the clippers for a clean fade on the sides?

​Do you have any sulfate-free shampoos or hair care products for colored hair?

​My scalp is quite sensitive, so please be gentle while washing my hair.

​How long will the hair coloring and blowout process take in total?

​Can I pay for the service using a credit card or mobile transfer?

​2. Hairstylist & Salon Staff

​Welcome to our hair salon! How can we help you transform your look today?

​Please take a seat right here, and I will put a protective cape around you.

​Are we doing just a haircut today, or would you like a shampoo wash as well?

​How much length would you like me to take off from the back and sides?

​Would you like your hair cut in straight layers or soft V-shaped layers?

​Let's look at our hair color chart together to pick the perfect shade for your skin tone.

​Your hair ends are quite dry and damaged; I recommend adding a hydrating keratin treatment.

​Would you prefer a side part or a middle part for your hairstyle today?

​How does this length look in the mirror? Should I go a little shorter?

​Please step over to the shampoo basin so we can wash and condition your hair.

​Is the water temperature comfortable for you, or would you like it warmer?

​I am going to apply a heat protectant serum before blow-drying your hair.

​Would you like me to style your hair straight or add some loose curls with the iron?

​Would you like some lightweight hair wax or hairspray to hold the style in place?

​You look fantastic! Here is a hand mirror so you can check the back of your hair.

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE: GETTING A HAIRCUT & COLOR CONSULTATION

​Stylist: "Good afternoon! Welcome to our salon. What are we doing for your hair today?"

​Customer: "Hi, good afternoon! I would like to get a haircut, and I am also thinking about coloring my hair."

​Stylist: "Great! Do you have a specific color in mind, or would you like to see our color catalog?"

​Customer: "I brought a photo on my phone. I am hoping to get a warm chestnut brown color."

​Stylist: "That is a beautiful color! Since your natural hair is dark brown, we can achieve this shade directly without bleaching."

​Customer: "That's fantastic! I want to avoid harsh bleaching if possible. What about the haircut?"

​Stylist: "How much length are you looking to cut off?"

​Customer: "Just about one inch off the bottom to clean up the split ends, and please add some long layers to give it movement."

​Stylist: "Understood. One inch trim with long layers and a warm chestnut brown dye. Let's start by applying the hair color first!"

​Customer: "Sounds like a plan. Thank you so much!"
