data.title: Bài 136: Các cuộc trò chuyện - Hoạt động quyên góp qua ứng dụng và hỗ trợ TuanQK English
data.transcript:
Conversations - App Donation & Community Support Practices (TuanQK English)

​1. For User & Community Supporter

​Good morning! I really love using the TuanQK English app for my daily language practice.

​How can I make a financial contribution or donation to support the development of TuanQK English?

​Are there any specific membership tiers or sponsor perks for monthly supporters of the app?

​Where can I find your official bank account details, QR code, or PayPal link to donate?

​Is there a minimum or maximum amount required when making a voluntary donation?

​Can I contribute by purchasing a premium ad-free subscription or buying in-app coffee items?

​How will the donated funds be utilized by the development team to improve the application?

​Will my name or profile be featured on the app's "Hall of Fame" or "Supporters" wall?

​Do you accept contributions via local bank transfers, Momo, ZaloPay, or international cards?

​Can I offer non-financial support, such as reporting bugs, writing reviews, or suggesting new content?

​Is it possible to set up an automated monthly recurring micro-donation to support ongoing server costs?

​Will I receive an official confirmation message or digital thank-you badge after making a donation?

​Can I sponsor a specific feature, such as new audio shadowing modules or advanced AI practice tools?

​Where can I track the app's development roadmap and public updates funded by community contributions?

​Thank you for creating such an amazing, free learning tool! Keep up the incredible work!

​2. Developer & App Support Team

​Welcome to TuanQK English! We are thrilled to hear that our app is helping you learn English every day.

​Your voluntary contributions help us cover server costs, cloud databases, and AI API operational expenses.

​You can easily donate by scanning the official QR code or using the bank transfer details inside the app settings.

​Every single contribution, no matter how small, directly powers new feature development and content updates.

​Supporters receive an exclusive "Gold Sponsor" badge on their profile and access to ad-free learning.

​We publish a transparent monthly breakdown of how community donations are allocated toward infrastructure and design.

​If you cannot contribute financially, leaving a 5-star review on Google Play or sharing the app with friends means the world to us!

​You can enter your name or personalized message in the transfer note to be featured on our "Community Champions" page.

​We accept local bank transfers, e-wallets, credit cards, and international payment options for your convenience.

​All supporters gain early access to closed beta features, including interactive AI conversation modules.

​Your generosity keeps TuanQK English free, accessible, and high-quality for learners all across the country.

​Please send us a screenshot of your transfer receipt so we can activate your supporter perks immediately.

​We are deeply grateful for your trust, encouragement, and dedication to growing this educational community together!

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE 1: INQUIRING ABOUT DONATION OPTIONS & PERKS

​User: "Hi Tuan! I have been using the TuanQK English app for two months now, and my speaking skills have improved so much. I want to contribute to help you keep developing it!"

​Developer: "Hello! Thank you so much for your kind words and encouragement! I am really glad to hear the app is helping you improve your English skills."

​User: "How can I send a donation to support the project? Are there official links or QR codes inside the app?"

​Developer: "Yes! You can go to the app's 'Settings' or 'Profile' tab and tap on 'Support TuanQK English'. You will see our QR, bank account details, and e-wallet links."

​User: "Great! What payment methods do you support for local users in Vietnam?"

​Developer: "We support direct transfers through all major Vietcombank banks, as well as international cards."

​User: "Awesome. Do supporters receive any special recognition or perks inside the app?"

​Developer: "Absolutely! Every supporter gets an ad-free experience, a special 'Sponsor' badge next to their username, and an invitation to our early beta test group!"

​User: "That sounds amazing! I will scan the QR code and send a contribution right now. Keep up the great work!"

​Developer: "Thank you so much for your generous support! It means a lot and helps us cover cloud database and AI API costs to keep the app growing!"

​DIALOGUE 2: CONFIRMING A CONTRIBUTION & BETA TESTING ACCESS

​User: "Hello! I just transferred 200,000 VND to support TuanQK English. Here is the screenshot of the transaction receipt."

​Developer: "Hello! Thank you so much! I just received the transfer notification. We truly appreciate your generous contribution!"

​User: "You're very welcome! How will these contributions be used for the upcoming app updates?"

​Developer: "The funds go directly into expanding our Supabase database bandwidth, upgrading our AI API tokens for real-time conversation practice, and adding new audio modules."

​User: "That's fantastic. I noticed the new AI speaking features in the roadmap. Can supporters test them early?"

​Developer: "Yes, definitely! I have just updated your account status to 'Gold Supporter'. You can now access the Closed Beta section in the app menu to test the AI voice chat tool."

​User: "Wow, that was super fast! I see the badge on my profile now. Thank you so much, Tuan!"

​Developer: "Thank you for being such an awesome part of our learning community! Please let me know if you have any feedback while trying out the new beta features!"

data.title: Bài 137: Các cuộc đối thoại - Tái trồng rừng & Các hoạt động lâm nghiệp
data.transcript:
Conversations - Reforestation & Forestry Practices

​1. For Forester, Environmentalist & Volunteer

​Good morning! We are holding a community tree-planting event to reforest this barren hillside today. 

​Which native tree species are we planting to restore the local biodiversity and soil stability?

​How deep should we dig the planting holes to accommodate the root systems of these young saplings?

​Please make sure to loosen the soil at the bottom of the pit and mix in natural organic compost.

​We need to install wooden stakes and protective mesh guards around the seedlings to prevent animal grazing.

​Are these bare-root saplings, or are they container-grown seedlings from the forestry nursery?

​How many saplings do we plan to plant per hectare to ensure optimal crown spacing and canopy cover?

​We must ensure proper watering and mulch application around the base to preserve soil moisture.

​Could you demonstrate the correct technique for removing the sapling from its biodegradable pot without damaging the taproot?

​We are monitoring the survival rate and growth metrics of last year's reforestation plot this afternoon.

​Are we utilizing natural regeneration techniques alongside artificial planting for this watershed protection area?

​Please ensure the root collar of the young tree stays flush with the surrounding soil level.

​How do we prevent soil erosion on steep slopes during the early establishment phase of the forest?

​We need to clear invasive weeds and brush away from the base of the saplings to reduce nutrient competition.

​What is the estimated rotation period and canopy closure timeline for this mixed-species forest stand?

​2. Forestry Manager, Nursery Specialist & Site Ranger

​Welcome to our forestry restoration site! Safety gloves and sturdy boots are required for field work.

​Today, we are planting indigenous hardwood species like oak, teak, and acacia to rebuild the forest canopy.

​Please keep a minimum distance of three meters between each planting spot along the contour line.

​Ensure the roots are spread out vertically in the pit and avoid bending them upward, which causes J-rooting.

​Firmly tamp down the soil around the seedling stem to remove air pockets, but do not overly compact it.

​Our nursery propagates thousands of disease-resistant saplings each season for regional afforestation projects.

​We apply a thick layer of organic woodchip mulch to suppress weed growth and retain ground moisture.

​Regular thinning and pruning will be required in five years to encourage strong vertical bole growth.

​We are establishing a protective riparian buffer zone along the riverbanks to prevent soil sedimentation.

​Firebreaks and cleared access trails are being maintained around the plantation perimeter to protect against forest fires.

​Community participation and long-term stewardship are essential for the sustainability of this reforestation program.

​Our target for this season is to plant fifty thousand trees across twenty-five hectares of degraded land.

​Please record the GPS coordinates and tree species tag numbers on your digital field survey app.

​All planted plots will undergo quarterly health checks and weed clearing during the first two years.

​Thank you for your hard work today! You are directly contributing to carbon sequestration and ecosystem renewal!

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE 1: TREE-PLANTING WORKSHOP & SAPLING PREPARATION

​Forester: "Good morning, everyone! Welcome to the watershed reforestation initiative. Today, we are planting two thousand native broadleaf saplings."

​Volunteer: "Good morning! I am excited to help. What native tree species will we be planting on this hillside today?"

​Forester: "We are using a mix of native oak and acacia saplings. This combination helps restore nitrogen levels in the soil and prevents landslide erosion."

​Volunteer: "That makes total sense. Could you show us how deep we should dig the holes?"

​Forester: "Certainly! Dig a pit about twice as wide as the seedling's root ball and slightly deeper. Make sure the soil at the bottom is loose."

​Volunteer: "Got it. How do we place the sapling into the ground correctly?"

​Forester: "Gently slide the root ball out of its container without pulling hard on the stem. Place it so the root collar is level with the soil surface, then backfill with topsoil."

​Volunteer: "Should we press down hard on the dirt around the base after planting?"

​Forester: "Press down gently with your hands to secure the plant and eliminate air pockets around the roots, but don't stomp on it. Finish with a bucket of water and a layer of mulch!"

​DIALOGUE 2: FORESTRY RESTORATION & SITE INSPECTION

​Environmental Inspector: "Good afternoon! I am conducting a site evaluation on the ten-hectare afforestation plot established last autumn."

​Forestry Manager: "Good afternoon! Welcome back. We've been tracking the plantation development closely over the past year."

​Environmental Inspector: "What is the current survival rate of the saplings across this section?"

​Forestry Manager: "Our latest inventory survey indicates a eighty-five percent survival rate, which exceeds our baseline target for this rough terrain."

​Environmental Inspector: "That's an excellent result! How are you managing weed competition and wild animal damage?"

​Forestry Manager: "We perform manual weeding twice a season and installed biodegradable mesh tree guards around the younger saplings to keep deer away."

​Environmental Inspector: "Very proactive! How is the canopy closure progressing in the denser trial blocks?"

​Forestry Manager: "The pioneer species are growing rapidly. We anticipate initial canopy closure within three to four years, which will naturally suppress shade-intolerant weeds."

​Environmental Inspector: "Fantastic work. Please make sure the firebreak lines around the northern boundary remain clear before the dry season begins."

​Forestry Manager: "Understood. Our maintenance team is scheduled to clear those perimeter firebreaks next week!"

data.title: Bài 141: Các cuộc hội thoại - Quy trình làm thủ tục tại sân bay
data.transcript:
Conversations - Airport Check-In Practices

​1. For Passenger & Traveler

​Good morning! I would like to check in for my flight to San Francisco, please.

​Here are my passport, visa documentation, and printed booking confirmation receipt.

​Could I please request a window seat near the front of the aircraft?

​Is an aisle seat available in the exit row for extra legroom on this long-haul flight?

​How many pieces of checked luggage am I allowed under my ticket class?

​Are my two checked bags checked all the way through to my final destination?

​Could you please mark this suitcase as fragile because it contains delicate electronics?

​How much is the excess baggage fee per kilogram if my luggage exceeds the weight limit?

​Can I carry my laptop bag and small backpack on board as my personal overhead items?

​Where are the liquid, aerosol, and gel restrictions specified for carry-on baggage?

​Could you please confirm the gate number and the exact boarding time for my flight?

​Is there a fast-track security lane available for business class or premium passengers?

​Can I purchase an upgrade to economy plus or business class at the counter today?

​Where is the airline lounge located, and does my transit pass grant access?

​What should I do if my connecting flight is delayed or rescheduled due to bad weather?

​2. Check-In Agent & Airline Ground Staff

​Good morning! Welcome to the airport check-in counter. May I please see your passport and flight booking details?

​Are you traveling alone today, or do you have any accompanying family members or travel partners?

​Please place your checked luggage flat onto the scale belt one bag at a time for weighing.

​I'm sorry, but your checked bag exceeds the twenty-three kilogram weight limit by three kilograms.

​Please make sure all lithium-ion batteries, power banks, and electronic devices are packed in your carry-on bag.

​Do you have any hazardous materials, flammable liquids, or sharp metal items inside your luggage?

​Here are your baggage claim tags; please keep them safe in case you need to identify your luggage.

​Your assigned seat is 14A, which is a window seat located in the forward section of the aircraft.

​Boarding will begin at gate B22 at four thirty PM, approximately forty minutes prior to departure.

​Please have your boarding pass and photo identification ready when passing through airport security and customs.

​You can scan the QR code printed on your boarding pass to receive real-time flight status notifications.

​The departure gate is a ten-minute walk from the main duty-free shopping area; please monitor gate changes.

​Please proceed through security screening and immigration control directly after completing check-in.

​Here is your original passport, boarding pass, and baggage claim receipts.

​Thank you for choosing our airline! We wish you a comfortable and pleasant flight!

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE 1: STANDARD CHECK-IN & SEAT PREFERENCE

​Check-In Agent: "Good morning! Welcome to Horizon Airlines. May I have your passport and booking reference, please?"

​Passenger: "Good morning! Here is my passport and my digital booking confirmation on my phone."

​Check-In Agent: "Thank you. I see you are booked on flight HA802 to Tokyo with a transfer to Los Angeles. Are you checking any bags today?"

​Passenger: "Yes, I have one large suitcase to check and one small carry-on backpack."

​Check-In Agent: "Please place your suitcase on the luggage scale... It weighs twenty-one kilograms, which is well within your limit. Do you have any power banks or lithium batteries inside this checked bag?"

​Passenger: "No, all my electronic devices and power banks are packed safely inside my carry-on backpack."

​Check-In Agent: "Perfect. Would you prefer a window seat or an aisle seat for the first leg of your flight?"

​Passenger: "An aisle seat toward the front of the plane would be great, please."

​Check-In Agent: "I have assigned you seat 12C, an aisle seat. Your checked luggage is tagged directly through to Los Angeles, so you won't need to collect it during your layover in Tokyo."

​Passenger: "That's very convenient! Thank you."

​Check-In Agent: "Here is your passport, boarding pass, and baggage claim ticket. Boarding starts at gate 18 at eight AM. Enjoy your flight!"

​DIALOGUE 2: HANDLING EXCESS BAGGAGE & GATE INFORMATION

​Check-In Agent: "Good afternoon, sir! Where are you flying to today?"

​Passenger: "Good afternoon! I am flying to London Heathrow on flight BA118."

​Check-In Agent: "May I see your passport and travel documents, please? Thank you. Please place your suitcase onto the scale."

​Passenger: "Here you go. I hope it isn't overweight!"

​Check-In Agent: "Let's see... Your bag weighs twenty-six kilograms. The standard allowance for your economy ticket is twenty-three kilograms."

​Passenger: "Oh dear! Can I pay for the three extra kilograms, or should I remove some heavy items into my hand luggage?"

​Check-In Agent: "You can either pay an excess baggage fee of thirty dollars per extra kilogram at the service desk, or repack up to three kilograms into your carry-on bag if space permits."

​Passenger: "I have space in my carry-on bag, so I'll quickly transfer my heavy jacket and books!"

​(After adjusting the bag weight)

​Passenger: "Okay, let's weigh it again!"

​Check-In Agent: "Now it reads exactly twenty-two point eight kilograms! Perfect. Here is your boarding pass for seat 24F. Boarding begins at gate C10 at six forty-five PM."

​Passenger: "Thank you so much for your patience and help!"

data.title: Bài 138: Conversations - House Cleaning & Housekeeping Practices
data.transcript:
Conversations - Household Chores & Family Cleaning Practices

​1. For Family Members (Parents, Children & Siblings)

​Could you please help me tidy up the living room before our guests arrive this afternoon?

​Whose turn is it to wash the dishes and clean the kitchen counter after dinner tonight?

​Please pick up your toys, storybooks, and clothes off the bedroom floor and put them away.

​Could you take out the trash bags and food waste to the recycling bins outside?

​Let's do a complete family deep clean of the whole house this Sunday morning!

​Can you sweep the kitchen floor while I mop the dining room and balcony?

​Please wipe down the dining table and clean up the food crumbs after finishing your snack.

​Don't forget to strip your bed sheets and pillowcases so we can wash them in the laundry machine.

​Could you help me fold the dry laundry and put your clothes into your closet drawers?

​Please scrub the bathroom floor and clean the mirror when you finish taking a shower.

​Can you vacuum the living room carpet and dust the television cabinet, please?

​Who left their wet towels on the sofa? Please hang them up on the drying rack outside.

​Could you organize your study desk and throw away all those old papers and broken pens?

​Let's clear out all the expired food and old leftovers from the refrigerator today.

​If we all work together and split the chores, we can finish everything in just one hour!

​2. Responses & Work Distribution Among Family Members

​I'll take care of washing the dishes and wiping down the kitchen stove right now.

​I'm already sweeping the living room; can someone else please mop the floor afterward?

​Mom, I just finished organizing my desk! Can I go play games after I take out the trash?

​Dad, where should I put these clean, folded towels? In the bathroom cabinet or the hallway closet?

​I'll go empty all the wastebaskets in the bedrooms and replace them with fresh bin liners.

​Let's divide the work: I'll clean the bathroom, you vacuum the bedrooms, and Dad cooks lunch!

​I've already put all my dirty clothes into the laundry basket in the washing room.

​Wait a minute, I am finishing my homework, then I will help with dusting the window sills.

​This grease stain on the kitchen counter is really tough; do we have any baking soda or spray cleaner?

​I just watered the indoor plants and wiped the dust off their leaves with a damp cloth.

​Don't worry, I'll hang the freshly washed clothes out on the clothesline to dry in the sun.

​All the shoes at the entryway are neatly arranged on the shoe rack now.

​I'm almost done vacuuming under the couch; watch out for your feet!

​The living room looks so bright, neat, and cozy now that we're all done!

​Great teamwork, everyone! Let's take a rest and enjoy some cold fruit juice!

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE 1: DIVIDING WEEKEND HOUSEHOLD CHORES

​Mom: "Good morning, everyone! Let's do a quick thirty-minute house cleanup before we go out today."

​Son: "Good morning, Mom! Sure. What would you like me to do first?"

​Mom: "Could you please pick up all your clothes and books in your bedroom, then vacuum the hallway?"

​Son: "Got it! I'll organize my bedroom right away. What about the living room?"

​Dad: "I'll handle the living room. I'm going to dust the TV stand, wipe the coffee table, and sweep the floor."

​Daughter: "Mom, can I help with the kitchen? I can wash the breakfast dishes and wipe down the counter."

​Mom: "That would be a huge help, sweetie! Thank you. I'll clean the bathroom and mop all the tiled floors."

​Dad: "Sounds like a solid plan! If we stick to our tasks, we'll be done in no time and can enjoy the rest of the weekend."

​Son: "Awesome! Let me turn on some music so we can clean faster!"

​DIALOGUE 2: CLEANING UP AFTER DINNER & LAUNDRY DUTIES

​Daughter: "Dinner was delicious tonight, Dad! Thanks for cooking."

​Dad: "You're very welcome! Now, whose turn is it on the chore chart to clear the dinner table tonight?"

​Son: "It's my turn tonight! I'll scrape the leftovers into the trash bin and load the dishes into the sink."

​Daughter: "I'll help you wipe the dining table and put the food containers back into the fridge."

​Dad: "Great teamwork, kids! While you two wrap up the kitchen, I'm going to sort the laundry."

​Mom: "Dad, please remember to separate the white clothes from the dark ones before starting the washing machine."

​Dad: "Will do! I'll also add some fabric softener so the towels come out nice and fluffy."

​Son: "Dad, after the laundry cycle is done, let me know so I can help hang the clothes on the drying rack."

​Dad: "Thanks, buddy! Once we finish everything, let me know what movie you all want to watch tonight!"

data.title: Bài 139: Các cuộc trò chuyện - Làm vườn & Các hoạt động chăm sóc sân vườn cùng gia đình
data.transcript:
Conversations - Gardening & Family Yard Work Practices

​1. For Family Members (Parents, Children & Siblings)

​Good morning, everyone! Let's spend some time taking care of our garden this morning.

​Could you please bring me the watering can and the garden trowel from the tool shed?

​Whose turn is it to water the vegetable patches and flower beds today?

​Please be careful when pulling out those weeds so you don't damage the roots of our young tomato plants.

​Can you help me mix some organic compost into the soil before we plant these flower seeds?

​Don't forget to put on your gardening gloves and hat before we go out under the sun.

​Could you grab the pruning shears and help me trim these overgrown hedge branches?

​Let's harvest some fresh herbs, sweet chili peppers, and green onions for tonight's dinner!

​Can you carry this bag of potting soil over to the flower pots on the patio?

​Look at these little strawberries ripening in the sun; we should put net covers over them to protect them from birds.

​Could you hold this wooden stake steady while I tie up the heavy tomato vines?

​Let's sweep up all the fallen leaves and twigs around the yard and throw them into the compost bin.

​Can you use the small rake to loosen the surface soil around the rose bushes?

​Please turn on the garden hose and wash off the dirt from the freshly picked carrots and radishes.

​Our yard looks so green, vibrant, and colorful now that we've all worked on it together!

​2. Responses & Task Sharing Among Family Members

​Dad, I'm filling up the watering cans right now! Should I water the potted orchids first?

​Mom, look! Our sunflowers have grown so tall, and there are small honeybees on the blossoms!

​I'll handle the weeding around the lettuce beds; there are quite a few unwanted weeds here.

​Where should I dump all these pulled weeds and dried leaves? In the green compost pit?

​I'm using the garden trowel to dig small holes for planting these new mint and basil seedlings.

​Dad, can you teach me how to prune these rose bushes without getting pricked by the thorns?

​I just checked the soil under the fruit trees; it feels a bit dry, so I'll give them a deep soak.

​Don't worry, Mom, I'll carefully pick the ripe tomatoes and put them in this basket.

​I've already swept the paved driveway and collected all the leaf debris into the lawn bag.

​Can someone hand me the garden hose? I want to spray off the dust on the patio tiles.

​Look, Dad! I found a earthworm in the soil! That means our soil is healthy, right?

​I'll carry the heavy bags of fertilizer back into the shed and lock up all the tools.

​I'm almost done trimming the grass along the border bricks with the edge trimmers.

​Everything in our family garden is thriving so well this season!

​Great work, everyone! Let me wash my hands and bring out some chilled lemonade for us to enjoy!

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE 1: PLANTING NEW SEEDLINGS & WEEDING THE GARDEN

​Mom: "Good morning, kids! The weather is lovely today. Let's head out to the backyard garden."

​Daughter: "Good morning, Mom! Yay! What are we planting in the garden today?"

​Mom: "We are going to plant some fresh basil seedlings and sow a row of cucumber seeds."

​Son: "Mom, where are the trowels and the gardening gloves? I want to help dig the holes!"

​Mom: "They are right inside the green basket by the shed door. Put on your gloves first, sweetie."

​Daughter: "Mom, look at all these wild weeds popping up around the strawberry patch!"

​Mom: "Good eye, dear! While your brother helps me dig holes for the basil, could you gently pull out those weeds by their roots?"

​Daughter: "Sure thing! I'll make sure to shake off the extra soil before tossing the weeds into the compost bucket."

​Son: "Mom, I dug three small holes here! Are these deep enough for the basil seedlings?"

​Mom: "That's perfect! Place one seedling in each hole, cover the roots with topsoil, and press down gently. Excellent job, team!"

​DIALOGUE 2: TRIMMING TREES & HARVESTING FRESH VEGETABLES

​Dad: "Hey kids, come check out the vegetable patch! Look how many ripe red tomatoes we have today!"

​Son: "Wow, Dad! They are so big and red! Can we harvest them for lunch today?"

​Dad: "Absolutely! Grab that wooden basket over there and pick the firmest, reddest ones."

​Daughter: "Dad, these chili pepper branches are getting really heavy and bending toward the ground."

​Dad: "Thanks for pointing that out. Let's insert a couple of bamboo stakes to support the branches so they don't break."

​Son: "Dad, can I help you prune the dead branches on the citrus tree with the small hedge shears?"

​Dad: "Of course, but let's do it together so you don't nip your fingers. Remember to cut at a slight angle near the stem."

​Daughter: "I've filled the entire basket with ripe tomatoes, sweet peppers, and fresh cilantro!"

​Dad: "Wonderful! Let's turn off the drip irrigation system, rinse off our tools, and head inside to wash these fresh vegetables!"

data.title: Bài 140: Các cuộc hội thoại - Thực hành phỏng vấn xin thị thực (Visa) tại Đại sứ quán
data.transcript:
Conversations - Embassy Visa Interview Practices

​1. For Visa Applicant

​Good morning, consular officer! I am here for my embassy visa interview.

​Here is my queue ticket, valid passport, completed visa application form, and passport photos.

​The main purpose of my visit is to attend a international business meeting and explore trade partnerships.

​I intend to stay for a duration of twelve days, departing on the fifth and returning on the seventeenth.

​I will be covering all travel, accommodation, and living expenses using my personal bank account and credit cards.

​Here are my certified bank statements for the past six months, income tax receipts, and asset ownership certificates.

​I run a software development business in my home country, which requires my full-time management upon return.

​All my immediate family members, including my parents and siblings, reside permanently in my home country.

​I have previously traveled to Japan, South Korea, and Singapore, and I have always strictly complied with visa regulations.

​Here is my confirmed round-trip flight reservation and hotel booking confirmation for the entire duration of my stay.

​I have also purchased comprehensive international travel insurance covering health and emergency evacuation.

​Here is the official invitation letter from the host organization, along with their registration details and event agenda.

​I have brought my original business registration license and proof of continuous commercial operations.

​Will my original supporting documents be returned to me immediately after the interview?

​Could you please confirm if my visa application requires any additional administrative processing?

​2. Consular Officer & Embassy Staff

​Good morning! Please step up to the counter and present your passport, appointment slip, and application documents.

​Please look directly into the camera in front of you for a digital facial photo verification.

​Please place your right hand four fingers flat on the fingerprint scanner, followed by your left hand.

​What specific products or services does your company specialize in, and what is your official job title?

​Who will be managing your business operations and team while you are away on this overseas trip?

​Do you have any relatives, close friends, or business associates who currently reside in our country?

​Can you explain the exact nature of your relationship with the host company that issued this invitation letter?

​Have you ever been convicted of any crime, or overstayed a visa in any foreign jurisdiction?

​Please show me your complete travel itinerary, including planned cities, internal transport, and scheduled meetings.

​How much liquid capital do you hold in your personal bank accounts to fund this travel?

​Why do you choose to travel at this specific time of the year instead of during peak holiday seasons?

​Please leave all electronic devices, smartwatches, and large bags in the security lockers outside the interview room.

​Your application has been approved! Your passport with the issued visa stamp will be sent to your registered address via express courier.

​We require additional administrative processing under our embassy immigration guidelines; we will keep your documents for review.

​Regrettably, we cannot grant you a visa today due to unestablished economic ties to your home country under our immigration law.

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE 1: EMBASSY BUSINESS VISA INTERVIEW & DOCUMENTS VERIFICATION

​Consular Officer: "Good morning! Please hand over your passport, appointment confirmation, and official invitation letter through the window."

​Applicant: "Good morning, officer! Here is my passport along with my complete application packet and supporting documents."

​Consular Officer: "Thank you. What is the primary purpose of your travel to our country?"

​Applicant: "I am traveling to attend an international technology exhibition and conduct preliminary business meetings with prospective software distribution partners."

​Consular Officer: "How long do you plan to stay, and where will you be staying during your visit?"

​Applicant: "I will be staying for ten days at the City Center Hotel. Here is my confirmed hotel booking voucher and round-trip flight itinerary."

​Consular Officer: "Can you tell me more about your current employment and financial background in your home country?"

​Applicant: "I am an independent software developer and business owner. Here are my company registration documents, tax clearances, and audited six-month bank statements."

​Consular Officer: "Have you held visas for other countries before?"

​Applicant: "Yes, I have previously held visas for Japan and South Korea for professional tech conferences, and I returned strictly within the permitted timeframe."

​Consular Officer: "Everything is completely in order. Your visa application is approved! You will receive your passport via courier within three to five business days."

​Applicant: "Thank you very much, officer! Have a wonderful day!"

​DIALOGUE 2: EMBASSY TOURIST VISA INTERVIEW & PROVING INTENT TO RETURN

​Consular Officer: "Good afternoon! Please place your right index finger on the optical scanner... Thank you. Why are you applying for a tourist visa today?"

​Applicant: "Good afternoon! I wish to travel as a self-guided tourist to visit historical landmarks, art museums, and cultural sites during my annual work leave."

​Consular Officer: "Are you traveling alone, or traveling with family members or an organized tour group?"

​Applicant: "I am traveling independently, but I have arranged a detailed day-by-day travel itinerary and booked local city tours in advance."

​Consular Officer: "Do you have any immediate family members, relatives, or close friends residing in our country?"

​Applicant: "No, officer. I have no relatives or acquaintances living abroad. My entire family lives here in my home country."

​Consular Officer: "What strong economic or social ties guarantee that you will return home after your vacation?"

​Applicant: "I have been employed as a senior technical developer with my current company for over five years, own my home, and my approved employer leave letter guarantees my return to work."

​Consular Officer: "May I review your employment verification letter and land title deeds?"

​Applicant: "Certainly! Here is my official employment certificate, salary payment records, and property ownership documents."

​Consular Officer: "Thank you for providing clear documentation. Your financial stability and intent to return are well established. Your visa is granted!"

​Applicant: "Thank you very much for your time and assistance, officer!"

data.title: Bài 142: Các cuộc hội thoại - Thủ tục cấp bằng lái xe & Bài thi lái xe thực hành
data.transcript:
Conversations - Driving License Procedures & Practical Driving Test

​1. For Driver Applicant & Trainee

​Good morning! I would like to submit my application for the Class B2 driver's license training course.

​What specific documents and health examination certificates are required for enrollment?

​Where can I register for the theoretical exam on road traffic rules and road signs?

​How many theory practice tests or simulation software modules do I need to complete before the test?

​Could you please explain the rules and scoring criteria for the closed-track yard driving test?

​What is the passing score required for both the theoretical exam and the practical yard test?

​I would like to practice parallel parking and reverse perpendicular parking on the practice track today.

​Could you please guide me on the correct procedure for stopping on an incline during the hill start test?

​How many kilometers of mandatory real-world road driving distance must be logged in the DAT system?

​What happens if my engine stalls or if the tire touches the curb line during the closed-track test?

​Could you please demonstrate how to operate the emergency light switch and emergency braking during the hazard signal event?

​How many days after passing the practical driving test will my physical driver's license card be issued?

​Is there a re-test fee if I fail either the theoretical exam or the practical driving evaluation?

​Could you please check my driving seat, side mirrors, and seatbelt adjustment before starting the vehicle?

​Thank you for your guidance, instructor! I am ready to begin the practical driving test track.

​2. Driving Instructor & Test Examiner

​Good morning! Welcome to the driver training center. Please present your identification card and application form.

​Please adjust your driver's seat, position your rearview mirrors, and fasten your seatbelt securely before starting the engine.

​Before moving off, turn on your left indicator light and wait for the examiner's start signal.

​Remember to disengage the handbrake completely before releasing the clutch pedal on the hill climb test.

​You must maintain a vehicle speed under twenty kilometers per hour while navigating the narrow S-curve maneuver.

​Points will be deducted automatically if your tires cross the sensor lines marked on the asphalt.

​When the emergency alarm sounds inside the cabin, stop immediately, turn on hazard lights, and turn them off only after the alarm ends.

​In the parallel parking section, ensure your vehicle is aligned parallel to the curb and within the yellow sensor boundary.

​For the simulated hazard scenario, stay calm, apply the foot brake firmly, and press the hazard warning button.

​During the road driving test, follow all traffic light signals, yield to pedestrians, and execute smooth gear shifts.

​You must accumulate eighty out of one hundred points to successfully pass the closed-track driving exam.

​Please review the electronic score printout on the dashboard display at the end of the test circuit.

​Congratulations! You have passed both the theoretical exam and the practical driving evaluation with high marks!

​Please sign your test results slip and proceed to the administrative counter for photo taking and license processing.

​Don't worry if you didn't pass today; you can register for a re-test scheduled for next fortnight.

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE 1: CLOSED-TRACK DRIVING TEST INSTRUCTION & HILL START

​Instructor: "Good morning! Are you ready for your B2 practical driving test simulation today?"

​Trainee: "Good morning, instructor! Yes, I'm a bit nervous, but I have practiced all eleven track maneuvers."

​Instructor: "That's completely normal. First, make sure your seat distance, steering wheel angle, and side mirrors are adjusted properly."

​Trainee: "Seat adjusted, mirrors set, and seatbelt fastened securely!"

​Instructor: "Great. Turn on your left indicator light. When you hear the start signal, release the handbrake and move forward slowly."

​Trainee: "Got it. Moving forward... The left indicator is off now after passing the start line."

​Instructor: "Good. The next obstacle is stopping on an incline for the hill start. Approach the stop line smoothly."

​Trainee: "Applying the clutch and foot brake... The bumper is aligned right above the stop line marker!"

​Instructor: "Perfect positioning! Now hold the handbrake, ease off the clutch until you feel the engine vibrate, then release the handbrake gently to climb without rolling back."

​Trainee: "Releasing the clutch... feel the bite point... releasing handbrake... and we're moving up smooth and clean!"

​Instructor: "Excellent execution! No rollback and zero points deducted. Keep moving toward the wheel track and narrow S-curve!"

​DIALOGUE 2: PARALLEL PARKING & COMPLETING THE PRACTICAL TEST

​Examiner: "You have completed seven track scenarios with ninety points remaining. Next up is parallel parking."

​Trainee: "Understood, examiner. Aligning the car parallel to the front reference line before reversing."

​Examiner: "Take your time. Keep an eye on your right side mirror and the rear sensor line."

​Trainee: "Reversing slowly at low clutch speed... turning the steering wheel fully to the right... now checking the left mirror for the rear corner marker."

​Examiner: "Good speed control. Keep backing up until the car is at a forty-five-degree angle."

​Trainee: "Straightening the wheels... reversing straight... turning left fully and backing into the slot..."

​(Beep sound from the automated sensor)

​Trainee: "The sensor confirm signal chimed! Realigning the wheels and shifting to first gear to exit the parking box."

​Examiner: "Clear exit without touching any curb sensors. Drive smoothly toward the finish line and turn on your right indicator."

​(Vehicle crosses the finish line)

​Examiner: "Test completed! Final score: ninety points out of one hundred. You passed the practical driving exam!"

​Trainee: "Thank you so much, examiner! I am so happy and relieved!"

data.title: Bài 143: Các cuộc trao đổi - Quy trình ghi danh và tuyển sinh học sinh tại trường học
data.transcript:
Conversations - School Enrollment & Student Admission Practices

​1. For Parent & Guardian

​Good morning! I am here to submit the enrollment application for my child for the upcoming school year.

​Could you please provide the list of required documents for enrolling a new student?

​Here are my child's birth certificate, household registration book, and official immunization records.

​What is the exact age requirement and cutoff date for entering the first grade this year?

​Could you please guide me on how to fill out the student personal information and emergency contact form?

​Are there any specific catchment area or residential proximity requirements for admission to this school?

​What are the school fees, including tuition, meal plans, uniform costs, and extracurricular activity fees?

​Does the school offer a school bus service with pickup and drop-off points near our neighborhood?

​Could we schedule a school tour to inspect the classrooms, library, playground, and cafeteria facilities?

​What specialized foreign language programs, STEM classes, or art clubs does the school provide?

​Is there a placement test or an informal interview process for incoming transfer students?

​How does the school handle student health care, medical emergencies, and dietary restrictions in the cafeteria?

​When will the official student class lists and homeroom teacher assignments be published?

​Could you please confirm the start date for the new academic orientation week and opening ceremony?

​Thank you so much for your warm support and guidance through this admission process!

​2. School Admission Officer & Administrator

​Good morning! Welcome to our school's admissions office. How may I assist you and your child today?

​Please submit certified copies of your child's birth certificate, health record book, and recent passport photos.

​Please make sure all emergency contact numbers and medical history details are clearly stated on the form.

​Our school follows a official curriculum combined with enhanced English and life skills programs.

​Tuition payments can be made per semester or for the full academic year through online bank transfer.

​School uniforms, physical education kits, and textbook bundles can be purchased at the administrative office.

​Our school cafeteria serves balanced, nutritious lunches with daily menu options catered to food allergies.

​We provide dedicated school bus routes with trained supervisors ensuring safe transit for all students.

​Homeroom teachers will conduct a brief, friendly meet-and-greet session with new students before the term begins.

​You will receive an official admission acceptance letter along with the orientation schedule via email.

​Please ensure all administrative fees and tuition deposits are settled prior to the orientation week.

​Parents can track their child's academic progress, daily attendance, and school announcements through our parent app.

​Here is your receipt and application tracking slip; your child's student ID number is generated on this form.

​We are delighted to welcome your child to our school community! We look forward to a fantastic school year!

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE 1: SUBMITTING ENROLLMENT DOCUMENTS & INQUIRING ABOUT SCHOOL FEES

​Parent: "Good morning! I would like to submit the primary school enrollment packet for my six-year-old son."

​Admission Officer: "Good morning! Welcome to our school. May I please see your child's application form and supporting documents?"

​Parent: "Here is the completed application form, certified birth certificate copy, household registration, and his health record."

​Admission Officer: "Thank you. Let me verify the documents... Everything is complete and properly certified! Is your family currently residing in the school's local catchment zone?"

​Parent: "Yes, our home is located about one kilometer from the school campus."

​Admission Officer: "Wonderful. That qualifies your child for priority admission. Here is the fee schedule breakdown for the first semester, including tuition, lunch, and boarding fees."

​Parent: "Thank you! Could you explain how the school meal service and afternoon boarding schedule work?"

​Admission Officer: "Students have a freshly cooked lunch prepared in our school kitchen, followed by a quiet nap time in the air-conditioned boarding rooms, and an afternoon light snack before dismissal."

​Parent: "That sounds very comfortable and well-organized! When should we complete the tuition payment?"

​Admission Officer: "You can pay through bank transfer or directly at the finance counter by the end of this week to confirm your child's place in Class 1A."

​DIALOGUE 2: SCHOOL TOUR & ACADEMIC CURRICULUM OVERVIEW

​Parent: "Hello! I am considering transferring my daughter to the fourth grade here. Could we learn more about the curriculum?"

​Admission Officer: "Hello! We would be delighted to show you around. Our fourth-grade curriculum balances academic subjects with STEM, art, and daily English practice with native teachers."

​Parent: "That sounds great! How many students are there in each class, and how do teachers interact with parents?"

​Admission Officer: "We maintain a maximum class size of thirty students to ensure personal attention. Teachers send weekly progress updates and daily notices through our mobile parent application."

​Parent: "Is there a placement assessment or interview for new transfer students?"

​Admission Officer: "Yes, we conduct a brief, stress-free foundational assessment in Math, Vietnamese, and English just to understand her learning level and assign her to the most suitable class."

​Parent: "Perfect! Can we take a quick tour of the classroom block and library today?"

​Admission Officer: "Of course! Right this way, please. I'll show you our computer lab, foreign language room, and green playground first."

data.title: Bài 122: Shadowing đàm thoại giao dịch ngân hàng
data.transcript:
1. Trong giao dịch ngân hàng và tài chính, việc phát âm chính xác các con số, đơn vị tiền tệ và thuật ngữ chuyên ngành là tối quan trọng để tránh nhầm lẫn, để thông tin giao dịch được truyền tải minh bạch, chuyên nghiệp.
2. Từ vựng ví dụ:
Transaction /trænˈzæk.ʃən/ (giao dịch)
Balance /ˈbæl.əns/ (số dư)
Withdrawal /wɪðˈdrɑː.əl/ (sự rút tiền)
Transfer /trænsˈfɝː/ (chuyển khoản)
Interest rate /ˈɪn.trɪst reɪt/ (lãi suất).
3. Câu thực hành: 
- I would like to transfer five hundred dollars to this account number.
- What is the current interest rate for a six-month savings plan?
- Please print a receipt for this withdrawal transaction.
4. Lưu ý: Luyện tập 5 lần, ghi âm và so sánh với mẫu. Giọng GA.

data.title: Bài 123: Shadowing họp nhóm qua Zoom / Google Meet
data.transcript:
1. Trong các cuộc họp trực tuyến, việc ngắt lời lịch sự, xin phát biểu hay tổng kết ý kiến đòi hỏi ngữ điệu rõ ràng, lịch thiệp nhưng dứt khoát để thu hút sự chú ý, qua thiết bị thu âm, mà không làm gián đoạn luồng thảo luận chung.
2. Từ vựng ví dụ:
Interrupt /ˌɪn.t̬əˈrʌpt/ (ngắt lời)
Microphone /ˈmaɪ.krə.foʊn/ (micrô)
Mute /mjuːt/ (tắt tiếng)
Summary /ˈsʌm.ɚ.i/ (tóm tắt, tổng kết)
Agenda /əˈdʒen.də/ (chương trình cuộc họp).
3. Câu thực hành: 
- Sorry to interrupt, but I would like to add a quick point here.
- Could you please turn on your microphone so everyone can hear you?
- Let me summarize the main key points before we end the meeting.
4. Lưu ý: Luyện tập 5 lần, ghi âm và so sánh với mẫu. Giọng GA.

data.title: Bài 144: Các đoạn hội thoại - Luyện phát âm tiếng Anh & phương pháp nhại theo Tuan & Lisa
data.transcript:
Conversations - English Pronunciation & Shadowing Practice (Tuan & Lisa)

​1. Tuan (Learner & Developer)

​Hey Lisa! Do you have a few minutes to help me refine my English pronunciation today?

​I am currently testing a new shadowing feature in my app, and I want to make sure my own speaking sounds natural.

​Could you listen to how I pronounce the short /ɪ/ and long /iː/ in words like "bit" and "beat"?

​I often struggle with the "th" sound in words like "algorithm," "database," and "method."

​Should my tongue touch my upper teeth or stick out slightly when producing unvoiced /θ/?

​How do I pronounce the final "-ed" ending in technical terms like "coded," "compiled," and "fetched"?

​Could you check if my word stress is correct when I say "developer," "repository," and "architecture"?

​When I speak fast, my intonation feels a bit flat. How can I add more natural sentence rhythm?

​Should I use rising intonation at the end of a question when asking for confirmation?

​How do native speakers link words together in phrases like "check it out" or "set it up"?

​Could you demonstrate how to pronounce the voiced /v/ sound versus the bilabial /w/ sound in "version"?

​Can you hear a clear distinction when I say "code" versus "coat" at normal speaking speed?

​I want to make sure my voice pitch drops properly at the end of declarative sentences.

​Could you repeat that sentence slowly so I can record your audio for my shadowing practice module?

​Thank you so much for practicing with me, Lisa! Your feedback is extremely helpful for my app!

​2. Lisa (Native Friend & Language Coach)

​Hi Tuan! I’d love to help you practice! It's always great to work on pronunciation together.

​Your app project sounds fantastic! Let's polish your spoken English so your audio recordings sound super clear.

​For the long /iː/ in "beat," smile slightly and hold the vowel sound a bit longer than in "bit."

​When making the unvoiced /θ/ in "method" or "algorithm," place the tip of your tongue lightly between your teeth.

​Great question! In "coded," the "-ed" adds an extra syllable /ɪd/, but in "compiled," it's just a soft /d/ sound.

​Let's check your word stress: in "de-VE-lo-per," stress the second syllable, and in "AR-chi-tec-ture," stress the first!

​To sound more natural, emphasize the key content words in a sentence while gliding over function words.

​Yes! Use rising intonation for yes/no questions, and falling intonation for statements or wh- questions.

​When connecting words, attach the final consonant of the first word to the opening vowel of the next—like "se-ti-tup"!

​For the /v/ sound in "version," gently rest your top teeth on your lower lip, whereas for /w/, round your lips into an "o" shape.

​Your final consonants are getting much clearer! Just make sure not to drop the unvoiced /t/ in "coat."

​Try lowering your pitch steadily on the last stressed syllable of your sentence to sound confident and conclusive.

​I'll read this technical paragraph at a steady pace so you can shadow my mouth movements and rhythm.

​You're doing an amazing job, Tuan! Your dedication to mastering spoken English is super inspiring!

​3. Dialogues

​DIALOGUE 1: TECHNICAL VOCABULARY & WORD STRESS PRACTICE

​Tuan: "Hi Lisa! Thanks for taking the time to practice with me today. I'm working on technical terminology for my language app."

​Lisa: "Hi Tuan! My pleasure! Technical terms can be tricky because of syllable stress. What words are you working on right now?"

​Tuan: "I want to check three words: 'developer', 'architecture', and 'repository'. Could you listen to how I say them?"

​Lisa: "Go right ahead! Say them one by one at your normal speed."

​Tuan: "Okay... 'de-ve-LOP-er', 'ar-chi-TEC-ture', and 're-po-si-TOR-y'."

​Lisa: "You nailed 'developer'! But for 'architecture', the primary stress is actually on the first syllable: 'AR-chi-tec-ture'. Try that one again."

​Tuan: "Ah, I see! 'AR-chi-tec-ture'... How was that?"

​Lisa: "Much better! And for 'repository', place the primary stress on the third syllable: 're-POS-i-tor-y'. Give it a shot!"

​Tuan: "Re-POS-i-tor-y... 'Architecture' and 'repository'!"

​Lisa: "Spot on, Tuan! The stress placement sounds completely natural now!"

​DIALOGUE 2: SENTENCE RHYTHM & CONNECTED SPEECH FOR SHADOWING

​Tuan: "Lisa, when I record audio lessons for my app, I want my sentence flow to sound smooth. How do you link phrases like 'push it up' or 'pull request'?"

​Lisa: "It's all about connected speech! When a word ending in a consonant meets a word starting with a vowel, they blend together effortlessly."

​Tuan: "So 'push it up' doesn't have three distinct pauses?"

​Lisa: "Exactly! The 'sh' in 'push' glides into 'it', and the 't' in 'it' turns into a light flap 'd' connecting to 'up'—so it sounds like 'pu-shi-dup'."

​Tuan: "Let me try shadowing you: 'pu-shi-dup'... 'push it up'!"

​Lisa: "Perfect! Now let's try a full sentence: 'I need to push it up to the repository.'"

​Tuan: "I need to... pu-shi-dup... to the re-POS-i-tor-y!"

​Lisa: "Awesome job, Tuan! Your speech rhythm is getting so smooth and natural. That recording will sound great in your app!"

data.title: Bài 145: Học 12 nguyên âm đơn cùng Tuan & Lisa
data.transcript:
Conversations - Learning 12 Monophthongs with Tuan & Lisa

1. For Tuan (Learner & Developer)

Hey Lisa! Today I want to focus on mastering all 12 English monophthongs (single vowel sounds).

Can we break them down into pairs of short and long vowels so I can practice my mouth shape and tongue position?

Let's start with the close front vowels: short /ɪ/ as in "kit" and long /iː/ as in "fleece."

How do I position my tongue and jaw for the close back vowels: short /ʊ/ in "foot" and long /uː/ in "goose"?

Next are the mid vowels: short /e/ in "dress," central schwa /ə/ in "about," and long /ɜː/ in "nurse."

Could you explain the open-mid back vowel /ɔː/ as in "thought" versus the short open back /ɒ/ as in "lot"?

What about the open front and central vowels: short /æ/ in "cat," short /ʌ/ in "strut," and long /ɑː/ in "father"?

How does the schwa sound /ə/ function in unstressed syllables across natural spoken English?

Could you listen to my pronunciation of "bit," "bet," "bat," and "but" to see if my jaw dropping is distinct?

Should my lips be rounded or unrounded when producing /uː/ versus /ɑː/?

Is there a noticeable difference in vowel length depending on whether the following consonant is voiced or voiceless?

Could you demonstrate the exact tongue height for the open vowel /æ/ compared to /e/?

I want to record your clear pronunciation of all 12 monophthong symbols for the IPA chart in my app.

Can we practice minimal pair sentences that combine these single vowel sounds together?

Thank you so much, Lisa! This step-by-step breakdown makes mastering English vowels so much easier!

---

2. For Lisa (Native Friend & Language Coach)

Hi Tuan! I’m thrilled to help you master all 12 English monophthongs step-by-step today!

Breaking them down by tongue position (front, central, back) and height (close, mid, open) is the best approach.

For /iː/ ("fleece"), spread your lips in a smile and raise your tongue high; for /ɪ/ ("kit"), relax your jaw slightly.

For /uː/ ("goose"), round your lips tightly and pull your tongue back; for /ʊ/ ("foot"), keep your lips loosely rounded.

For /e/ ("dress"), drop your jaw halfway; for /ə/ ("about"), keep your mouth completely neutral and relaxed.

For /ɜː/ ("nurse"), keep your tongue neutral in the center and hold the sound; it’s the long version of the central vowel family.

For /ɔː/ ("thought"), round your lips and push your tongue back; for /ɒ/ ("lot"), open your mouth wider with short duration.

For /æ/ ("cat"), open your mouth wide and flatten your tongue; for /ʌ/ ("strut"), keep your mouth slightly less open and central.

For /ɑː/ ("father"), drop your jaw fully to the lowest position and keep your tongue flat at the back.

The schwa /ə/ is the most common sound in English! It only occurs in unstressed syllables, like the "a" in "about."

Let's do the jaw-drop test: as you move from /iː/ to /e/ to /æ/, your lower jaw should drop progressively lower!

Always remember: long vowels (/iː/, /uː/, /ɜː/, /ɔː/, /ɑː/) have a colon symbol /ː/ in IPA and are held longer in time.

I will read all 12 vowels with example words slowly so you can record pristine audio for your TuanQK English app!

Let's practice minimal pairs right now to build your muscle memory for every single sound!

---

3. The 12 Monophthongs Summary Table

| IPA Symbol | Vowel Type | Key Word | Mouth & Tongue Position |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **/iː/** | Long Close Front | **fleece** /fliːs/ | Lips smiling, tongue high front, long duration |
| **/ɪ/** | Short Close Front | **kit** /kɪt/ | Lips relaxed, jaw slightly dropped, short duration |
| **/e/** | Short Mid Front | **dress** /dres/ | Jaw half-open, lips spread loosely |
| **/æ/** | Short Open Front | **cat** /kæt/ | Jaw open wide, tongue flat and low in front |
| **/ʌ/** | Short Open-Mid Central | **strut** /strʌt/ | Mouth relaxed, jaw mid-open, short central sound |
| **/ɑː/** | Long Open Back | **father** /ˈfɑːðə/ | Jaw fully dropped, mouth wide open, tongue back |
| **/ɒ/** | Short Open Back | **lot** /lɒt/ | Mouth open wide, lips slightly rounded, back sound |
| **/ɔː/** | Long Mid-Back | **thought** /θɔːt/ | Lips rounded into an 'O', tongue pulled back |
| **/ʊ/** | Short Close Back | **foot** /fʊt/ | Lips loosely rounded, short duration |
| **/uː/** | Long Close Back | **goose** /ɡuːs/ | Lips tightly rounded, tongue high back |
| **/ɜː/** | Long Mid Central | **nurse** /nɜːs/ | Mouth neutral, relaxed tongue in center, long sound |
| **/ə/** | Short Mid Central (Schwa) | **about** /əˈbaʊt/ | Completely neutral mouth, unstressed, short & weak |

---

4. Dialogues

DIALOGUE 1: FRONT VOWELS & THE JAW-DROP TECHNIQUE (/iː/, /ɪ/, /e/, /æ/)

Tuan: "Lisa, I want to test the four front vowels in order: /iː/, /ɪ/, /e/, and /æ/. Can you guide my mouth positioning?"

Lisa: "Sure thing, Tuan! Think of this group as a ladder going from high to low jaw position. Start with /iː/ as in 'fleece'."

Tuan: "Okay... /iː/... 'fleece', 'see', 'beat'."

Lisa: "Perfect! Your lips were smiling and tongue was high. Now drop your lower jaw just a tiny bit for the short /ɪ/ in 'kit'."

Tuan: "/ɪ/... 'kit', 'sit', 'bit'."

Lisa: "Great contrast! Now drop your jaw halfway for /e/ as in 'dress'."

Tuan: "/e/... 'dress', 'set', 'bet'."

Lisa: "Spot on! Now for the lowest one, /æ/ as in 'cat', open your mouth wide like you're at the doctor's office!"

Tuan: "/æ/... 'cat', 'sat', 'bat'! Let me do all four in a row: 'beat' - 'bit' - 'bet' - 'bat'!"

Lisa: "Wow, Tuan! That sequence was absolute perfection! Your jaw dropped gradually on each sound exactly as it should!"

---

DIALOGUE 2: CENTRAL & BACK VOWELS PRACTICE (/uː/, /ʊ/, /ɔː/, /ɒ/, /ɑː/, /ʌ/, /ɜː/, /ə/)

Tuan: "Now let's tackle the back and central vowels! I often get confused between /ɔː/ in 'thought' and /ɒ/ in 'lot'."

Lisa: "That's very common! For /ɔː/ in 'thought', round your lips tightly into a small circle and hold the vowel long. For /ɒ/ in 'lot', open your mouth wider with short duration."

Tuan: "Let me try: /ɔː/... 'thought', 'bought', 'cord'. And /ɒ/... 'lot', 'spot', 'cod'."

Lisa: "Excellent! You can really hear the length difference and lip shape change. Now let's test /uː/ versus /ʊ/."

Tuan: "/uː/ in 'goose' has tight rounded lips... 'goose', 'boot', 'fool'. And /ʊ/ in 'foot' is short... 'foot', 'book', 'full'."

Lisa: "Nailed it! What about the schwa /ə/ and /ɜː/?"

Tuan: "The schwa /ə/ is completely relaxed, like in 'a-bout' or 'teach-er'. And /ɜː/ is held longer in 'nurse', 'bird', 'work'."

Lisa: "Fantastic job, Tuan! You have all 12 monophthong positions down pat. Your IPA lesson in the app is going to be incredibly clear!"

data.title: Bài 146: Học 8 nguyên âm đôi cùng Tuan & Lisa
data.transcript:
Conversations - Learning 8 Diphthongs with Tuan & Lisa

1. For Tuan (Learner & Developer)

Hey Lisa! Today I want to learn all 8 English diphthongs (double vowel sounds) in detail.

Could you explain how a diphthong works as a smooth glide from one vowel position to another?

Let's divide them into three categories: centering diphthongs ending in /ə/, closing diphthongs ending in /ɪ/, and closing diphthongs ending in /ʊ/.

First, how do I pronounce the centering diphthongs: /ɪə/ in "ear," /eə/ in "air," and /ʊə/ in "cure"?

Next, let's practice the closing diphthongs ending in /ɪ/: /eɪ/ in "bay," /aɪ/ in "buy," and /ɔɪ/ in "boy."

What about the closing diphthongs ending in /ʊ/: /əʊ/ in "no" and /aʊ/ in "now"?

Should the first starting vowel sound be longer and stronger than the second ending sound in every diphthong?

How can I avoid breaking a diphthong into two separate monophthongs when speaking at normal speed?

Could you check my lip rounding and tongue glide when moving from /a/ to /ʊ/ in words like "house" and "out"?

What is the difference between the British /əʊ/ and the American /oʊ/ in words like "go" and "boat"?

Can you hear a clear contrast when I say "ear" /ɪə/, "air" /eə/, and "are" /ɑː/?

I want to record your clear pronunciation of all 8 diphthong symbols for the IPA chart in my app.

Could you listen to my pronunciation of "take," "time," "coin," "go," and "cow" to verify my vowel glides?

Can we practice minimal pair sentences containing multiple diphthong sounds back-to-back?

Thank you so much, Lisa! Mastering these 8 diphthongs will make my app's phonetic lessons complete!

---

2. For Lisa (Native Friend & Language Coach)

Hi Tuan! I’m excited to help you master all 8 English diphthongs step-by-step today!

A diphthong is a single syllable vowel sound where your mouth glides continuously from the first starting position to the second target position.

Always remember: about 75% of the duration and stress goes to the first vowel, while the second vowel is shorter and lighter!

For the centering diphthongs (/ɪə/, /eə/, /ʊə/), your tongue always glides toward the neutral central schwa /ə/ sound.

For /ɪə/ ("ear"), start at /ɪ/ ("kit") and glide smoothly to /ə/ ("about"); for /eə/ ("air"), start at /e/ ("dress") and move to /ə/.

For /ʊə/ ("cure"), start with rounded lips at /ʊ/ ("foot") and relax into schwa /ə/.

For closing diphthongs ending in /ɪ/ (/eɪ/, /aɪ/, /ɔɪ/), your jaw closes slightly as your tongue moves up toward /ɪ/.

For /eɪ/ ("bay"), move from /e/ to /ɪ/; for /aɪ/ ("buy"), open wide at /a/ and glide up; for /ɔɪ/ ("boy"), start rounded at /ɔː/ and move up.

For closing diphthongs ending in /ʊ/ (/əʊ/, /aʊ/), your lips round as your mouth glides toward /ʊ/.

For /əʊ/ ("go"), start at neutral schwa /ə/ and round into /ʊ/; for /aʊ/ ("now"), open wide at /a/ and pull back into /ʊ/.

Don't pause or interrupt the airflow between the two vowel positions—keep the movement smooth and fluid!

I will demonstrate each sound slowly so you can capture pristine audio recordings for your TuanQK English app!

Let's run through interactive dialogues and minimal pairs right now to lock in your muscle memory!

---

3. The 8 Diphthongs Summary Table

| IPA Symbol | Diphthong Type | Key Word | Glide Movement & Mouth Position |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **/ɪə/** | Centering (to /ə/) | **ear** /ɪə/ | Glides from close front /ɪ/ to neutral schwa /ə/ |
| **/eə/** | Centering (to /ə/) | **air** /eə/ | Glides from mid front /e/ to neutral schwa /ə/ |
| **/ʊə/** | Centering (to /ə/) | **cure** /kjʊə/ | Glides from rounded /ʊ/ to neutral schwa /ə/ |
| **/eɪ/** | Closing (to /ɪ/) | **face** /feɪs/ | Glides from mid front /e/ up to close front /ɪ/ |
| **/aɪ/** | Closing (to /ɪ/) | **price** /praɪs/ | Glides from open /a/ wide jaw up to close /ɪ/ |
| **/ɔɪ/** | Closing (to /ɪ/) | **boy** /bɔɪ/ | Glides from rounded /ɔː/ up to close front /ɪ/ |
| **/əʊ/** | Closing (to /ʊ/) | **goat** /ɡəʊt/ | Glides from central schwa /ə/ to rounded /ʊ/ |
| **/aʊ/** | Closing (to /ʊ/) | **mouth** /maʊθ/ | Glides from wide open /a/ to rounded back /ʊ/ |

---

4. Dialogues

DIALOGUE 1: CENTERING DIPHTHONGS PRACTICE (/ɪə/, /eə/, /ʊə/)

Tuan: "Lisa, let's practice the three centering diphthongs first: /ɪə/, /eə/, and /ʊə/. How should I transition between the vowels?"

Lisa: "Keep in mind that all three end at the neutral schwa /ə/. Start strong on the first vowel, then relax your mouth toward the center. Try /ɪə/ as in 'ear'."

Tuan: "Okay... /ɪə/... 'ear', 'near', 'here'."

Lisa: "Great! Your starting sound /ɪ/ was strong, and you relaxed nicely into /ə/. Now try /eə/ as in 'air'."

Tuan: "/eə/... 'air', 'pair', 'care'."

Lisa: "Notice how your jaw starts a little lower for /e/ before moving to schwa! Now try /ʊə/ in 'cure'."

Tuan: "/ʊə/... 'cure', 'pure', 'tour'."

Lisa: "Excellent rounding on the lips to start! Now listen to the contrast in a single phrase: 'Clear air in a pure tour'!"

Tuan: "'Clear air in a pure tour'... /ɪə/ - /eə/ - /ʊə/!"

Lisa: "Spot on, Tuan! You articulated every single glide smoothly without chopping the vowels!"

---

DIALOGUE 2: CLOSING DIPHTHONGS PRACTICE (/eɪ/, /aɪ/, /ɔɪ/, /əʊ/, /aʊ/)

Tuan: "Now let's tackle the closing diphthongs! Why are they called 'closing' diphthongs?"

Lisa: "Because your lower jaw moves upward and your mouth closes slightly as you glide toward /ɪ/ or /ʊ/. Let's try /eɪ/, /aɪ/, and /ɔɪ/ first!"

Tuan: "/eɪ/ in 'face', 'make', 'day'... /aɪ/ in 'price', 'my', 'time'... and /ɔɪ/ in 'choice', 'boy', 'coin'."

Lisa: "Fantastic articulation! The jaw glide from wide open /a/ up to /ɪ/ in 'time' was super clean. Now let's try the two ending in /ʊ/: /əʊ/ and /aʊ/."

Tuan: "/əʊ/ in 'goat', 'no', 'code'... and /aʊ/ in 'mouth', 'now', 'out'."

Lisa: "Perfect lip rounding as you finish on /ʊ/! Let's combine them all into one sentence: 'They found five gold coins out by the lake.'"

Tuan: "'They /eɪ/ found /aʊ/ five /aɪ/ gold /əʊ/ coins /ɔɪ/ out /aʊ/ by the lake /eɪ/'!"

Lisa: "Amazing job, Tuan! You mastered all 8 diphthongs with flawless transitions! That completes the entire IPA vowel set for your app!"

data.title: Bài 147: Học 24 phụ âm cùng Tuan & Lisa
data.transcript:
Conversations - Learning 24 Consonants with Tuan & Lisa

1. For Tuan (Learner & Developer)

Hey Lisa! Today I want to focus on mastering all 24 English consonant sounds to complete the full IPA chart for my app.

Can we organize the 24 consonants into logical pairs based on voiced and unvoiced sounds?

Let's start with the 8 stop/plosive consonants: /p/ vs /b/, /t/ vs /d/, /k/ vs /g/.

How do I position my tongue for the dental fricatives: unvoiced /θ/ in "think" versus voiced /ð/ in "this"?

What about the labiodental fricatives: unvoiced /f/ in "fan" versus voiced /v/ in "van"?

How do we distinguish the alveolar fricatives /s/ and /z/ from the postalveolar fricatives /ʃ/ in "shoe" and /ʒ/ in "vision"?

Could you explain the two affricate sounds: unvoiced /tʃ/ in "church" versus voiced /dʒ/ in "judge"?

What are the 3 nasal consonants: /m/ in "man," /n/ in "now," and /ŋ/ in "sing"?

How do I produce the glottal fricative /h/ and the lateral approximant /l/ in "light"?

Could you demonstrate the proper tongue positions for the approximants: /r/ in "red," /w/ in "wet," and /j/ in "yes"?

How can I train my throat muscles to feel the vocal cord vibration on voiced consonants?

Why do native speakers puff out a small burst of air (aspiration) on /p/, /t/, and /k/ at the beginning of words?

I want to record your audio samples for all 24 consonant symbols to embed into the TuanQK English app modules.

Can we practice minimal pairs that compare tricky voiced and unvoiced pairs like /v/ and /w/, or /θ/ and /s/?

Thank you so much, Lisa! Having all vowels, diphthongs, and consonants mapped out makes our English library complete!

---

2. For Lisa (Native Friend & Language Coach)

Hi Tuan! I’m excited to help you master all 24 English consonants today!

Grouping them by voicing (voiced vs unvoiced) and manner of articulation (plosives, fricatives, affricates, nasals, approximants) is the most efficient way to learn!

Unvoiced consonants use only air pressure without vocal cord vibration, while voiced consonants require your vocal cords to vibrate!

For plosives (/p/ vs /b/, /t/ vs /d/, /k/ vs /g/), you block airflow completely and then release it in a small burst!

Remember: initial /p/, /t/, and /k/ are aspirated in English, meaning you should feel a distinct puff of air on your hand!

For dental fricatives (/θ/ vs /ð/), rest the tip of your tongue gently between your front teeth and blow air through.

For postalveolar sounds (/ʃ/ vs /ʒ/), round your lips slightly and push your tongue back—like telling someone to be quiet ("shh")!

For affricates (/tʃ/ vs /dʒ/), combine a stop with a fricative—start with your tongue on the roof of your mouth and release into a hiss!

For the nasal sound /ŋ/ ("sing"), lower your soft palate and let the sound resonate through your nose without touching your tongue tip to the roof!

For /r/, curl your tongue slightly back without touching the roof of your mouth, and for /j/ ("yes"), start near the close vowel /iː/ position!

Place your hand on your throat while practicing: if you feel a buzzing vibration, it's voiced; if you feel only air, it's unvoiced!

I will record all 24 consonant sounds clearly with example words so your app learners get crystal-clear audio!

Let's jump into our practice dialogues and minimal pairs right now!

---

3. The 24 Consonants Summary Table

| IPA Symbol | Manner & Place | Voice Status | Key Word | Production Technique |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **/p/** | Bilabial Plosive | Unvoiced | **pen** /pen/ | Press lips together, release air burst (aspirated) |
| **/b/** | Bilabial Plosive | Voiced | **bad** /bæd/ | Press lips together, release with vocal vibration |
| **/t/** | Alveolar Plosive | Unvoiced | **tea** /tiː/ | Tongue tip on alveolar ridge, release air burst |
| **/d/** | Alveolar Plosive | Voiced | **did** /dɪd/ | Tongue tip on alveolar ridge, release with vibration |
| **/k/** | Velar Plosive | Unvoiced | **cat** /kæt/ | Back of tongue against soft palate, release air |
| **/g/** | Velar Plosive | Voiced | **got** /ɡɒt/ | Back of tongue against soft palate, release with vibration |
| **/f/** | Labiodental Fricative | Unvoiced | **fall** /fɔːl/ | Top front teeth on bottom lip, blow air |
| **/v/** | Labiodental Fricative | Voiced | **van** /væn/ | Top front teeth on bottom lip, vibrate vocal cords |
| **/θ/** | Dental Fricative | Unvoiced | **thin** /θɪn/ | Tongue tip between teeth, blow air without voice |
| **/ð/** | Dental Fricative | Voiced | **this** /ðɪs/ | Tongue tip between teeth, vibrate vocal cords |
| **/s/** | Alveolar Fricative | Unvoiced | **see** /siː/ | Tongue near alveolar ridge, hiss air through teeth |
| **/z/** | Alveolar Fricative | Voiced | **zoo** /zuː/ | Tongue near alveolar ridge, buzz vocal cords |
| **/ʃ/** | Postalveolar Fricative | Unvoiced | **shoe** /ʃuː/ | Rounded lips, tongue pulled back, "shh" air |
| **/ʒ/** | Postalveolar Fricative | Voiced | **vision** /ˈvɪʒn/ | Rounded lips, tongue pulled back, buzzing "zh" |
| **/tʃ/** | Postalveolar Affricate | Unvoiced | **chain** /tʃeɪn/ | Stop air with tongue then release into "sh" |
| **/dʒ/** | Postalveolar Affricate | Voiced | **jam** /dʒæm/ | Stop air with tongue then release into buzzing "zh" |
| **/h/** | Glottal Fricative | Unvoiced | **hat** /hæt/ | Open throat, breathe out friction air |
| **/m/** | Bilabial Nasal | Voiced | **man** /mæn/ | Lips closed, sound resonates out through nose |
| **/n/** | Alveolar Nasal | Voiced | **now** /naʊ/ | Tongue on alveolar ridge, sound out through nose |
| **/ŋ/** | Velar Nasal | Voiced | **sing** /sɪŋ/ | Back of tongue raised to palate, nasal airflow |
| **/l/** | Lateral Approximant | Voiced | **leg** /leɡ/ | Tongue tip touches alveolar ridge, air flows past sides |
| **/r/** | Post-alveolar Approximant | Voiced | **red** /red/ | Tongue curled back slightly, no contact with roof |
| **/w/** | Labio-velar Approximant | Voiced | **wet** /wet/ | Lips rounded into tight "o", glide into vowel |
| **/j/** | Palatal Approximant | Voiced | **yes** /jes/ | Tongue raised high near hard palate, quick glide |

---

4. Dialogues

DIALOGUE 1: PLOSIVES, ASPIRATION & VOICING PAIRS (/p/, /b/, /t/, /d/, /k/, /g/)

Tuan: "Lisa, let's test the 6 plosive consonants in pairs: /p/ vs /b/, /t/ vs /d/, and /k/ vs /g/. How can I test my aspiration?"

Lisa: "Hold your hand about two inches in front of your mouth! When you say unvoiced /p/, /t/, and /k/, you should feel a distinct puff of air hit your palm."

Tuan: "Let me try... /p/... 'pack'... Wow, I felt the air! And /b/... 'back'..."

Lisa: "Notice how on 'back', there was no puff of air, but your vocal cords in your neck vibrated! Now try /t/ vs /d/."

Tuan: "/t/... 'time' (lots of air!)... /d/... 'dime' (vocal cords buzzing!)."

Lisa: "Spot on! Now test the velar pair at the back of your mouth: /k/ vs /g/."

Tuan: "/k/... 'coat'... /g/... 'goat'!"

Lisa: "Flawless! You have complete control over plosive aspiration and throat voicing now!"

---

DIALOGUE 2: FRICATIVES & AFFRICATES PRACTICE (/θ/, /ð/, /v/, /w/, /ʃ/, /ʒ/, /tʃ/, /dʒ/)

Tuan: "Now let's practice the tricky fricatives and affricates, especially /θ/ vs /ð/ and /v/ vs /w/!"

Lisa: "For /θ/ in 'think' and /ð/ in 'this', put your tongue tip between your teeth. /θ/ is just blowing air, while /ð/ adds vocal buzz!"

Tuan: "/θ/... 'think', 'thank', 'three'... and /ð/... 'this', 'that', 'there'."

Lisa: "Perfect tongue placement! Now for /v/ vs /w/: for /v/ in 'van', touch your top teeth to your lower lip. For /w/ in 'win', round your lips like a circle!"

Tuan: "/v/... 'van', 'vine', 'very'... and /w/... 'wan', 'wine', 'every'!"

Lisa: "Great contrast! Finally, let's do affricates /tʃ/ in 'chip' and /dʒ/ in 'gym'."

Tuan: "/tʃ/... 'cheap', 'church'... and /dʒ/... 'jeep', 'judge'!"

Lisa: "Fantastic work, Tuan! You've mastered all 24 consonants! Combined with our 12 monophthongs and 8 diphthongs, your English library has the complete 44 IPA sound set!"
